Reopening condition recorded: a measured registry cost that matters, or a native API that requires the user pointer to be the object itself.
5. **True call-site varargs** — declined for v1 ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)); the v2 candidate if per-arity aliases proliferate in real bindings.
6. **Foreign-thread registration** for long-lived embedder threads — deferred with item 1's blocker (b).
7. **Inline arrays of C-compatible records** (`[N]R`) as record fields and extern parameters — a recorded liftable v1 bound ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types), [§32.13](#sec-c-compatible-records)): C struct-array fields exist in the wild; lifting is layout work plus tests on §32.13's engine, no new mechanism.
8. **First-class runtime library loading** (program-controlled `dlopen`-style loading and binding of extern blocks, deferring [§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)'s startup resolution): subsumed by items 1–2's runtime questions. (Binding `dlopen`/`dlsym` themselves through the FFI as opaque `IntPtr` handles remains expressible, [§32.7](#sec-pointers-and-intptr); what is deferred is calling the resolved pointers — item 2.)

---

<a id="sec-program-entry-point"></a>
## 33. Program Entry Point

<a id="sec-the-main-method"></a>
### 33.1 The `Main` method

Every Bezel executable has exactly one entry point: a `public static method Main` declared on a class in the **root compilation** ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly)) — with several qualifying candidates permitted only under [§33.5](#sec-program-entry-point-resolution)'s explicit disambiguation. The **main module** is the module containing the selected entry point (when the root compilation is an import SCC of several modules ([§2.5](#sec-dependency-resolution)), every member module's classes are searched — the build-target rule; several candidates across members are the ordinary [§33.5](#sec-program-entry-point-resolution) conflict). A qualifying signature in a dependency artifact is **inert** ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly) rule 3): never selected, never a conflict, an ordinary method. The runtime locates the entry point and invokes it to start the program.

<a id="sec-accepted-signatures"></a>
### 33.2 Accepted signatures

```bezel
public static method Main()
public static method Main(args: Array<string>)
public static method Main(): int
public static method Main(args: Array<string>): int
public static async method Main(): Task
public static async method Main(args: Array<string>): Task
public static async method Main(): Task<int>
public static async method Main(args: Array<string>): Task<int>
```

A signature outside this set does not qualify as an entry point; a method named `Main` with a non-qualifying signature is an ordinary method.

For the `async` forms, the runtime drives `Main`'s task as the main domain's first continuation and blocks the **startup thread** — which runs outside any domain ([§30.13](#sec-runtime-model)) — until the task settles; the pool's workers drain the main domain meanwhile. This is the mechanism [§30.3](#sec-the-task-taskt-and-ownedtaskt-types) cites: the one legitimate blocking wait, at the process edge.

`Main` must be `public` and `static`. An instance method named `Main` does not qualify.

<a id="sec-exit-code"></a>
### 33.3 Exit code and termination

When `Main` returns `int` or `Task<int>`, the returned value becomes the process exit code. Otherwise, normal completion produces an exit code of 0.

**Uncaught exception:** an exception escaping `Main` (or the awaited `Main` task faulting) produces exit code **70** (the conventional software-error code, matching `EX_SOFTWARE`), after the runtime prints the exception's type, message, stack trace, and `CauseChain` ([§31.4](#sec-standard-exception-types)) to standard error. The [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order) shutdown sequence (static `owned` disposal) still runs.

**Live domains at exit:** when `Main` completes, spawned domains that have not completed are **abandoned**: the runtime signals no cancellation, runs no further continuations of theirs, and proceeds to the shutdown sequence — their owned state is reclaimed by the process exit, not by disposal, and their pending effects are lost. A program that needs a spawned domain's work must join it (await its completion task) before returning; the abandonment rule makes `Main`'s return the single authoritative end of computation rather than introducing an implicit barrier. In-flight continuations of the **main** domain queued behind `Main`'s completion are likewise not run.

**`Environment.Exit(code)`:** callable from any domain; it initiates the same shutdown sequence (no further continuations anywhere, static `owned` disposal on the dedicated shutdown thread, then process exit with `code`). It never returns. Like abandonment above, it is a statement that remaining work is deliberately discarded.

<a id="sec-command-line-arguments"></a>
### 33.4 Command-line arguments

The `args` parameter, when present, contains the command-line arguments. The program's own executable path is not included; `args[0]` is the first user-supplied argument.

`args` is typed `Array<string>` (the heap-allocated form, [§15.2](#sec-heap-arrays)). This matches the rest of the standard library, where collection-typed parameters are uniformly `Array<T>` or an `IList<T>`/`IEnumerable<T>` interface. The runtime constructs `args` once at program entry and does not mutate it; users who want fixed-size discipline simply do not call resize methods on it.

Programs that want to forward args to a method expecting `IEnumerable<string>` or `IList<string>` can pass `args` directly. Programs that need a specifically-sized inline buffer (for FFI marshalling, for example) construct a fresh inline array from the args' contents.

<a id="sec-program-entry-point-resolution"></a>
### 33.5 Resolution

A program is ill-formed if more than one method qualifies as the entry point. This applies both across classes (multiple classes each declaring a qualifying `Main`) and within a single class (one class declaring more than one of the eight signature shapes from [§33.2](#sec-accepted-signatures)). The search space is the root compilation only ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly)): a qualifying `Main` in a dependency artifact is inert and never conflicts.

For the cross-class case, the build tool must accept a `--main-class FullyQualifiedName` flag (or its equivalent in tool-specific configuration); the named class is selected as the entry point and a successful build ensues. Without disambiguation, the compiler produces an error listing every qualifying `Main` it found.

For the within-class case, no flag-based disambiguation is provided: a class may declare at most one qualifying `Main`. A class that overloads `Main` with multiple qualifying signatures is rejected at compile time with a clear error pointing to the ambiguous overloads. (A class may still declare a non-qualifying `Main` alongside a qualifying one — for example, an instance method named `Main` does not qualify, so it does not conflict.)

The exact CLI surface is implementation-defined — different tools may use `--main`, `--entry-point`, project-file properties, or other surfaces — but every conforming implementation must expose a mechanism semantically equivalent to "name the fully-qualified class whose `Main` to use." The flag name `--main-class` and its accepted argument shape (a fully-qualified type name) are normative for tools that use a command-line interface.

<a id="sec-example"></a>
### 33.6 Example

```bezel
module HelloWorld;

class Program
  public static method Main(args: Array<string>)
    if args.Count > 0 then
      Console.WriteLine($"Hello, {args[0]}!");
    else
      Console.WriteLine("Hello, Bezel!");
    end;
  end Main;
end Program;
```

A library build has no entry point ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly)); a qualifying `Main` in a library compilation is an ordinary method.

---

<a id="sec-comments-and-documentation"></a>
## 34. Comments and Documentation

Three comment forms ([§1.5](#sec-comments)):

- `// ...` line comment.
- `/* ... */` block comment, does not nest.
- `/// ...` documentation comment.

Documentation comments use XML element syntax. Recognized tags include `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<paramref>`, `<typeparam>`, `<typeparamref>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>`, `<remarks>`, `<example>`, `<see>`, `<seealso>` (`<typeparam>`, `<typeparamref>`, and `<paramref>` — generic declarations are documented like any other). The compiler preserves them in output metadata for documentation generators; it does not interpret tag content beyond preservation. Unrecognized tags are preserved verbatim in the same metadata: recognition affects only how documentation tooling may render a tag, never compilation.

Documentation comments are meaningful only immediately before a declaration.

```bezel
/// <summary>
/// Represents a bank account with deposit and withdrawal functionality.
/// </summary>
public class BankAccount: IBankAccount
  /// <summary>
  /// Deposits the specified amount into the account.
  /// </summary>
  /// <param name="amount">The amount to deposit. Must be positive.</param>
  /// <exception cref="ArgumentException">Thrown when amount is non-positive.</exception>
  public method Deposit(amount: decimal)
    if amount <= 0m then
      throw new ArgumentException("Amount must be positive.", nameof(amount));
    end;
    Balance := Balance + amount;
  end Deposit;
end BankAccount;
```

<a id="sec-choices"></a>
## 35. Choices

A **choice** is a closed nominal sum: a value type whose values are drawn from a fixed, named set of **cases**, where each case may carry a positional payload. Conceptually it sits between enums (closed, named, no payloads) and records (field products, no case discrimination). Construction is qualified (`FetchOutcome.Failed(504, "upstream timeout")`) — or bare in a declared-result position ([§35.3](#sec-choice-construction)); consumption is `case` with positional destructuring and full static exhaustiveness ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness) — no `_` arm needed when every case is covered). *(the section is numbered here to preserve every existing section number and anchor — its conceptual home in the [§3.1](#sec-type-kinds) kind ordering is between enums and classes.)*

```bezel
public choice FetchOutcome
  Fetched(owned response: Response),      // owned class payload
  NotModified,                            // payload-free case
  Failed(status: int, message: string);   // value payloads

  public method IsSuccess(): bool => (case this of
    Fetched(_)   => true,
    NotModified  => true,
    Failed(_, _) => false);
end FetchOutcome;
```

<a id="sec-choice-declaration"></a>
### 35.1 Declaration

Each value of a choice type has exactly one **active case** at a time; the active case determines which payload components the value carries. A case declares zero or more positional **payload fields**, each `Identifier ":" Type` with an optional leading `owned` marker; a case with no payload list is **payload-free**. Case names are PascalCase by convention and must be distinct within the choice; a case name may not collide with any member name of the choice (the [§11.3](#sec-member-body) member rules apply with cases counted as members). A choice declares at least one case. Choices are implicitly sealed and cannot derive from any type; a choice may implement interfaces ([§35.8](#sec-choice-boxing)). Choices cannot have destructors, constructors, instance fields, block-form or storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types — the same restriction set as enums ([§10.5](#sec-restrictions)), for the same reasons, plus one: a choice's instance storage *is* its cases' payloads, declared in the case list and reachable only through matching.

A choice payload field may not, directly or transitively through value-typed components (record fields, inline-array elements, other choices' payloads), have the declaring choice's own type: a value type cannot contain itself. Recursive sums are expressed with a class node in the cycle (an `owned` class payload whose class holds the nested choice), exactly as recursive records are.

The `owned` payload marker's admissibility follows [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s type requirement verbatim: admissible on class types, interface types, and bare type parameters; admitted-but-redundant on move-only value types; a compile error on any other type. For a **bare type parameter** payload the marker follows §28.1's per-instantiation erasure — the payload slot is owned at class and interface substitutions and the marker is erased at value and runtime-managed substitutions. Case-payload position is among §28.1's admissible positions.

<a id="sec-choice-members"></a>
### 35.2 Members

A choice body may declare, after the case list, exactly what an enum body may ([§10.4](#sec-methods-properties-static-members), grammar A.4 `EnumMember`): instance methods, expression-bodied read-only properties, static methods, static readonly fields (including `static owned readonly`), `const` members, and operator overloads. `this` in a choice instance method is a **borrow** of the receiver value; owned-consuming operations through `this` are rejected — the same reasoning as [§19.3](#sec-patterns)'s move-only scrutinee rule (a method invocation must not silently consume its receiver), and for a generic choice this keeps method-body checking independent of the instantiation's classification ([§35.11](#sec-choice-generics)). Choice methods are statically dispatched; `virtual`/`abstract`/`override` are rejected as on enums ([§10.5](#sec-restrictions)), and §10.5's `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/`ToString` plain-member replacement rule carries over for the boxable classifications.

A choice has no user constructors, instance fields, or storage-backed properties by design: a choice's construction *is* case selection — a user constructor would have to pick a case, which the qualified case form already spells — and independent instance storage alongside the payload union would make every value part-product-part-sum, destroying the one-active-case invariant that exhaustiveness and disposal both lean on.

**Compiler-provided per-instantiation members (v0.233).** The standard library's `Result<T, E>` (stdlib [§2.20](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-result)) carries four **compiler-provided** value-payload combinators — `Map`, `MapError`, `AndThen`, `UnwrapOr` — declared in its own listing and admissible **only where the receiver instantiation and the member's result instantiation are both value-like** ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification) rule 3) — for `Map<U>`/`AndThen<U>` the result is `Result<U, E>`, for `MapError<F>` it is `Result<T, F>`, so a call whose inferred `U` or `F` would make the result instantiation borrow-bearing or owning is rejected exactly as a call on such a receiver is; the rejection lands at the use site under [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2, the diagnostic naming the classification, the deciding payload, and the owning-match remedy ([§35.5](#sec-choice-matching)). These members stand outside [§35.11](#sec-choice-generics)'s once-and-classification-independent body discipline — their bodies are compiler-provided and exist only where the members are admissible — on the compiler-known-standard-library footing of [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)'s behavior-dispatch reservation and the compiler-provided-conformance precedent of [§11.8](#sec-static-interface-members); a user-declared choice method cannot be conditioned on the instantiation's classification.

<a id="sec-choice-construction"></a>
### 35.3 Construction and payload ownership

Construction is qualified, resolving exactly as enum constants do ([§10.1](#sec-basic-syntax)): `FetchOutcome.NotModified` for a payload-free case (a value expression, not a call), `FetchOutcome.Failed(504, "upstream timeout")` for a payload case. Within a `case` over a choice scrutinee the prefix may be omitted in patterns ([§35.5](#sec-choice-matching)); in expression position outside a **declared-result position** (below) the qualified form is required, exactly as for enum constants outside their scrutinee. For a **generic** choice the type arguments are written at the construction (`Result<int, string>.Ok(value)`): [§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference)'s posture — type-level arguments are never inferred from constructor arguments — extends to case construction unchanged.

**Declared-result target-typing (v0.233).** In a **declared-result position** — the top-level operand of a `return e;` statement in a body with a declared return type ([§21.7](#sec-the-return-statement)); the expression body of a member or accessor checked against a declared type ([§22.2](#sec-expression-bodied-methods), [§23.2](#sec-expression-bodied-read-only-properties), [§23.3](#sec-block-form-properties), indexers per [§23.4](#sec-indexers)); or a `return e;` statement or expression body checked against a lambda's **return-type ascription** ([§27.3](#sec-lambda-expressions)) — where the declared type — for an `async` body, the declared `Task<T>`'s result type, per [§30.1](#sec-async-methods)'s completion rule — nullability stripped, is a **choice instantiation** `C<…>` (or non-generic choice `C`) that declares a case named `N`: the form `N(args)` is a **case construction** of `C<…>.N(args)`, and the bare identifier `N` is the payload-free case value `C<…>.N`. The declared type supplies the choice type and all its type arguments whole; nothing is inferred from the construction's arguments ([§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference)'s posture above is untouched), and partial qualification does not join the family — `Result.Ok(v)`, the generic type with no arguments, remains an error; the admitted spellings are the fully qualified form and the bare case name. Payload-argument binding and ownership are exactly the qualified form's (below): the form is resolved to a case construction before classification or any ownership rule runs. A declared nullable `C<…>?` target-types through the stripped form and the result converts by [§5.1](#sec-implicit-conversions)'s `T → T?` wrapping. The rule reads the declared type **as written**, with the enclosing declaration's type parameters rigid: it does not fire on a bare type parameter (`method M<R>(): R` declares no choice), while a written choice instantiation inside a generic body (`method M<T>(): Result<T, string>`) fires normally; a non-`async` method declared over a `Task`-family type returns a task, not a choice, so the case reading never fires in its body. When the declared type is not a choice, or is a choice without a case of the written name, the form is an ordinary expression under ordinary resolution — nothing changes. Within a declared-result position whose type *is* such a choice, the case reading is **authoritative**: it wins over any same-named local, parameter, member, or type in scope, and the compiler warns on such shadowing — naming the case and the shadowed declaration, with the remedy (qualify the intended member call, bind its result to a differently-named local first, or rename the shadowed binding — a local or parameter cannot be qualified). A payload case written bare, or a payload-free case written with an argument list, is the arity error [§35.5](#sec-choice-matching) names on the pattern side. The qualified construction remains valid everywhere.

The case reading does not extend beyond the written-declared-type family: not to lambdas whose return type arrives only by target inference (no ascription written), not to argument position (the [§17.7](#sec-the-new-operator) `new()` shorthand draws the same line), not to `var` initialization, typed local declarations, field initializers, or default parameter values, and not to subexpression positions within a return operand — in `return (if c then Ok(v) else Error(e));` the branches are operands of the `(if …)` atom ([§20](#sec-the-if-expression)) and resolve ordinarily; write two `return` statements, or the qualified form. (A redundant parenthesized grouping around the whole operand — `return (Ok(v));` — is transparent for this purpose.) Outside the family a bare case-named form keeps its ordinary resolution (or its ordinary-resolution error); when that error arises in a body whose declared result type is a choice with the written case name, the diagnostic carries a note naming the two remedies (move the construction to a declared-result position, or qualify it).

```bezel
// Declared-result positions: the declared type supplies Result<int, string> whole.
public method ParsePercent(text: string): Result<int, string>
  if not int.TryParse(text, out var value) then
    return Error($"not a number: {text}");   // = Result<int, string>.Error(…)
  end;
  if value < 0 or value > 100 then
    return Error($"out of range: {value}");
  end;
  return Ok(value);                          // = Result<int, string>.Ok(…)
end ParsePercent;

public method CachedOutcome(): FetchOutcome => NotModified;   // bare payload-free case value
```

Payload arguments bind to the case's payload fields as to a parameter list, and the `owned` payload marker has exactly an `owned` parameter's call-site semantics ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers), [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)):

```bezel
var resp := new Response(headers, stream);
return FetchOutcome.Fetched(move resp);       // call-site marker; resp is moved-from after
```

- An argument to an **owned payload slot** is an owned-consuming position (the [K3.3](#sec-kernel-k3) `owned`-argument position): a fresh producer or unbound owned temporary transfers with no marker (no live binding is invalidated); a named owned binding requires the [§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers) call-site marker (`move resp`) and is left moved-from; the consume-site freeze ([K5](#sec-kernel-k5)) rejects the transfer while a live local borrow of the binding exists.
- An argument to a **plain class- or interface-typed payload slot** is a borrow, and [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s **no-temporary-source rule** applies verbatim: constructing a borrow-bearing choice from a temporary bound to a borrow-carrying payload is rejected (bind the source to a named local first).
- Value, `string`, and runtime-managed payload arguments copy or share per their type kinds.

The constructed value's own ownership follows its classification ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)): a value-like construction is an ordinary value; a borrow-bearing construction is a borrow-carrying value under §9.7's rules; an owning construction is an **owned move-only value** — [§28.3](#sec-producers)'s producers rows for move-only values cover it (the caller takes ownership and discharges by binding, storing, returning, or consuming it), and a construction not bound to any name is an unbound owned temporary under [K8](#sec-kernel-k8)'s full-expression machinery.

A method returning an owning choice writes the plain type (`method Fetch(url: string): FetchOutcome`); `owned` on the return is admitted-but-redundant per [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s move-only clause, exactly as for owning inline arrays.

<a id="sec-choice-classification"></a>
### 35.4 The classification

The **choice classification** is a derived type property ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)) computed from the payload fields of *all* the choice's cases:

1. A choice is **owning** if any case has a payload field marked `owned` (a class, interface, or — at a class or interface instantiation — bare-type-parameter payload), or a payload field of a move-only value type ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types) — an owning inline array or another owning choice, transitively).
2. Otherwise, a choice is **borrow-bearing** if any case has a *borrow-carrying* payload field, under exactly [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s definition: a plain (unmarked) field of class or interface type (nullable or not); an inline-array field with reference-typed elements; a borrow-bearing record; or — transitively — a borrow-bearing choice.
3. Otherwise the choice is **value-like**: every payload is a value, a `string`, a runtime-managed type, or (transitively) a value-like record or choice. A value-like choice is an ordinary copyable value type.

Payloads of runtime-managed reference types (`string`, function types, boxed values) are classification-neutral, exactly as in [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal): such values have unbounded lifetime by construction.

**Borrow-bearing choices** are subject to [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)'s borrow-lifetime rules through [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s bullet list, applied verbatim with "record" read as "record or choice": a borrow-bearing choice value may not outlive any carried borrow's source; may not be constructed from a temporary source; may not be stored in a class instance field or (outside the null-source form) a static field; is constrained in returns, closures, and collection copies; and is forbidden as an `async` method's parameter or result ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods)). A live local of borrow-bearing choice type counts as a live local borrow of every carried borrow's source for the consume-site freeze ([K5.5](#sec-kernel-k5)), exactly as for records.

**Owning choices are move-only value types** ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)). Every §15.3 rule applies as written: local-to-local assignment moves (unmarked — copies are impossible, so there is nothing for a marker to disambiguate); parameter passing is by value-move; return transfers; a move-only value may be a class field (the class's destructor disposes it) and may not be a record field; locals are auto-disposed at scope end with the must-use warning ([K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3)); exception edges discharge implicitly ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3)); `using var` is admitted with pin-only effect. And the async seam is closed on the owning side as on the borrow-bearing side: no [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal) producer row admits a move-only value result, so a `Task<T>` or `OwningTask<T>` declared over an owning choice is a compile error at the declaration — for generic declarations, re-checked after substitution at the instantiation site ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal), [§35.11](#sec-choice-generics)). Two owning-choice rules are *stronger* than the owning-inline-array precedent, deliberately:

- **Disposal is defined by the active case.** Disposing an owning choice value disposes the active case's `owned` payloads (in payload declaration order) and, recursively, any move-only payloads; payload-free and value-payload cases dispose nothing. There is no per-slot moved-from state to consider: payloads are reachable only through matching, never as assignable slots — the value is always wholly owned or wholly moved-from.
- **Drop-on-overwrite is defined and automatic** (derives: [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3)). Whole-value reassignment of an owning-choice local or field *disposes the displaced value* per [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields), like an owned class binding — **not** like [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)'s owning-inline-array reassignment rule (the warning-backed manual discipline): that rule exists because an inline array's slots can be individually moved-from, leaving a partial state the compiler cannot cheaply dispose, and a choice has no partial states, so the sound automatic behavior is available and taken. Reassignment is a consume of the displaced value and is frozen while borrows of it live ([K5.2](#sec-kernel-k5)). `x := null;` on an owned `C?` location likewise disposes the displaced value's payloads ([§35.9](#sec-choice-nullable)).

<a id="sec-choice-matching"></a>
### 35.5 Matching

<a id="sec-choice-borrowing-match"></a>
#### The borrowing match (the default)

Matching a choice value **non-destructively** is the default everywhere, and [§19.3](#sec-patterns)'s rules apply verbatim: a pattern binding is a borrow whose source is the scrutinee's source; the scrutinee retains its ownership state; the construct never moves from the scrutinee. For a value-like choice, payload bindings are copies (value payloads) or shared references (`string`/runtime-managed payloads); for borrow-bearing and owning choices, class-typed payload bindings are borrows. An **unmarked read of a named owned binding in scrutinee position stays a borrowing match** — [§19.3](#sec-patterns)'s move-only scrutinee rule, now load-bearing: it is what makes *peeking* at an owned outcome legal and non-consuming.

```bezel
var outcome := client.Fetch(url);       // owned move-only local
case outcome of                          // borrowing match; outcome unchanged
  Failed(var s, _) when s >= 500 => ScheduleRetry(),
  _                              => ()
end;
// outcome is still owned here; discharge or auto-drop per §28.3.
```

<a id="sec-owning-match"></a>
#### The owning match

An **owning match** transfers the selected case's `owned` payloads into the arm's bindings and consumes the scrutinee value. It is triggered in exactly two scrutinee forms — both *announced*, in the [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows) sense that something at the site tells the reader the value is consumed:

1. **An unbound owned temporary** of owning-choice classification — a fresh construction, an owning-choice-returning call, a `move` result. This is the dominant shape and needs no marker, as fresh producers never do:

   ```bezel
   case client.Fetch(url) of                 // owning match over the temporary
     Fetched(var r)       => RenderOwned(move r),    // r: owned Response in the arm
     NotModified          => RenderCached(),
     Failed(var s, var m) => ShowError(s, m)
   end;
   ```

   The scrutinee temporary's full expression is the **whole `case` construct** — [K8.3](#sec-kernel-k8), applied unchanged — so payloads not transferred into bindings (discarded slots like `Fetched(_)`, and the payloads of the value when a `_` or non-destructuring arm is selected) are disposed when the construct completes, by the same unbound-temporary pass that disposes the container. An exception out of an arm disposes the not-yet-consumed remainder during unwinding ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3)).

2. **A named owned binding under an explicit scrutinee transfer marker** — `case move outcome of …`, the scrutinee an identifier-operand `move` expression ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression); derives: [K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3)'s marked-transfer family; frozen per [K5.1](#sec-kernel-k5)). This is the marker discipline ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows) *Move semantics for owned locals*) extended to scrutinee position, with its exact rules: the marker is required because the unmarked read is a borrow (above), an unmarked read never silently consumes, the marker on a borrowed or fresh-producer scrutinee is an error, and the consumed binding is left **moved-from** when the construct completes. Because the transfer hands payloads **alive** to the arm's bindings — no disposed flag is set, nothing faults — the consume is frozen while a live local borrow of the binding's value exists, precisely the reasoning that froze the owning-iterator `yield return` ([§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership)) and left Pattern B `await` unfrozen ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal) sets the disposed flag; this construct does not). *(The scrutinee marker is not redundant here, though move-only values move unmarked into owning stores ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types); [K3.12](#sec-kernel-k3)): scrutinee position has an unmarked borrow reading to disambiguate, so the marker carries meaning.)*

   ```bezel
   var outcome := client.Fetch(url);
   case move outcome of                      // marked consume; outcome moved-from after `end`
     Fetched(var r) => do
       using var resp := move r;             // adopt: scope-bound disposal (§28.10)
       Render(resp);
     end,
     NotModified          => RenderCached(),
     Failed(var s, var m) => ShowError(s, m)
   end;
   ```

In an owning match, an `owned`-payload binding (`var r` above) is an **owned local of the arm body's scope**, and [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)'s standard rules apply to it on every arm-exit edge — the [§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership) owning-iteration-variable model: falling off the arm still owning the value auto-drops it with the must-use warning naming the binding and the standard remedies (`using var u := move r;` adoption in a `do … end` arm, an owned-consuming call, an explicit `r.Dispose()`, `_ := r;`); exception edges discharge implicitly. In *expression-position* arms (which cannot contain statements, [§19.2](#sec-arms)), the warning-free discharges are an owned-consuming call (`RenderOwned(move r)`) or §19.2's helper-method extraction. Value payloads bind as copies; discarded owned slots (`Fetched(_)`) are disposed at construct completion as above. Nested destructuring of an owned payload does not arise: owned payloads are class- or interface-typed, and classes do not destructure ([§19.3](#sec-patterns)).

**What does not trigger an owning match:** an unmarked named-binding scrutinee (borrowing, above); a borrowed scrutinee of any provenance (field read, parameter, `this`); and the position of the *construct's result* — whether the `case`'s value flows into an owned slot is the [§28.3](#sec-producers) arm-meet row's business and has no bearing on how the scrutinee is consumed.

<a id="sec-owning-match-guards"></a>
#### Guards: borrow during trial, transfer on selection

In an owning match, pattern bindings are **borrows of the scrutinee's payloads during pattern matching and guard evaluation**; ownership transfers into the selected arm's bindings **when an arm is selected** (its pattern matched and its guard, if any, evaluated true). A guard therefore observes borrows and cannot consume a binding (owned-consuming positions reject a borrow); after selection, the arm body sees the bindings in their owning-match states.

If **no arm** of an owning match selects: in statement position the construct completes with no action and the consumed value's payloads are disposed at construct completion (the value was consumed by the announced form; its contents have nowhere to go); in expression position `MatchFailureException` is raised ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)) and the payloads are disposed during unwinding by the standard exception-path machinery. Exhaustive matches — the normal case — never reach either.

<a id="sec-case-patterns"></a>
#### Case patterns

- A **payload-free case** is matched by its bare name (`NotModified`) — a constant-style pattern resolving through the scrutinee-type prefix-omission rule, extended from enums ([§10.6](#sec-case-matching), [§19.8](#sec-inside-enum-scrutinees)): within a `case` whose scrutinee is a choice, the choice prefix may be omitted. A name resolving to a case is a case pattern, never a type test.
- A **payload case** is matched by a positional destructuring pattern `CaseName(slot, …)` with the case's exact payload arity — grammar A.7's existing destructuring production. All [§19.3](#sec-patterns) slot rules carry over: naked identifiers bind, `var x` binds explicitly, `_` discards per slot, per-slot `|` alternatives among binding-free members, nested patterns recurse.
- A payload case's slots may equivalently be matched **by name** — `Fetched(response = var r)` — resolving the case's payload field names ([§19.3](#sec-patterns) *Named destructuring*, [§35.1](#sec-choice-declaration)); the slot list is positional or named, never mixed. All the same slot rules carry over. The borrowing match binds payload borrows and the owning match does **not** transfer through a named slot (a named-matched owned payload is borrowed during the arm and disposed at construct completion, [§19.3](#sec-patterns)); a program wanting the payload transferred writes the positional destructure.
- A payload case may **not** be matched bare: `Fetched` without parentheses is a compile error naming the arity — matching a payload while ignoring it is spelled visibly as `Fetched(_)`, the same explicitness §19.3 demands of record destructuring arity.
- Payload-free case names are admissible members of `|` **alternative lists** (and count toward exhaustiveness, [§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)); payload-carrying case patterns are not, even in the all-discard form — they are destructurings, not constants ([§19.3](#sec-patterns)).

<a id="sec-owning-match-traces"></a>
#### Disposal traces (the four paths of an owning match)

All four paths ride existing machinery; none introduces a new disposal-site kind.

**(a) Normal path, payload bound and adopted.**

```bezel
case client.Fetch(url) of
  Fetched(var r) => do
    using var resp := move r;    // r moved into resp; resp disposed at arm-body end
    Render(resp);
  end,
  NotModified          => RenderCached(),
  Failed(var s, var m) => ShowError(s, m)
end;
```

The scrutinee temporary is produced owned; arm selection transfers the payload's ownership into `r`; the adopt idiom moves it into `resp`, disposed at the `do … end` block's close; the container value, now payload-empty, is reclaimed at construct completion with nothing left to dispose. Exactly one disposal of the payload, at a statically known site.

**(b) Normal path, payload discarded.**

```bezel
case client.Fetch(url) of
  Fetched(_)  => Count("hit"),     // owned payload never bound
  _           => Count("other")
end;
```

The `Fetched(_)` discard binds nothing; the payload stays with the consumed scrutinee value and is disposed at construct completion by the unbound-temporary pass — the "disposal runs after every use within the expression" ordering [K8.1](#sec-kernel-k8) defines. The `_` arm on a `NotModified`/`Failed` value disposes nothing (those cases carry no owned payloads).

**(c) Guard-declined path.**

```bezel
case move outcome of
  Fetched(var r) when r.IsStale() => do _ := r; RefetchLater(); end,
  Fetched(var r)                  => do using var resp := move r; Render(resp); end,
  _                               => ()
end;
```

During the first arm's guard, `r` is a **borrow** — `r.IsStale()` is an ordinary borrowing call, and a consuming use in the guard would be rejected. If the guard declines, no transfer has happened; the second arm's selection performs it. Two arms binding the same payload are two candidate *recipients*, not two owners: transfer happens once, at selection.

**(d) Exception path.**

```bezel
case move outcome of
  Fetched(var r)       => do Validate(r); Publish(move r); end,    // Validate may throw
  NotModified          => (),
  Failed(var s, var m) => throw new UpstreamException(m)
end;
```

If `Validate(r)` throws, `r` — an owned local of the arm-body scope — is disposed by the exception-path discharge ([K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3)) exactly as any owned local is; the consumed scrutinee (already payload-transferred) has nothing further to dispose. If the `Failed` arm's `throw` runs, that case's payloads are values and need no disposal; an owned payload in a throwing arm is covered by the same unwind pass. The moved-from `outcome` binding is skipped by every pass, as always.

<a id="sec-choice-diagnostics"></a>
#### Diagnostics

Per [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 4, the new errors name the classification and the rule. Recommended messages:

- *"Payload case `Fetched` requires a payload pattern: write `Fetched(...)` with 1 slot, or `Fetched(_)` to discard."*
- *"`case move` requires a named owned binding of an owning choice type as its scrutinee; `x` is borrowed."* / *"… is a fresh producer, which needs no marker."*
- *"Cannot consume `outcome` here: the borrow held by `b` (declared at line N) is still live."* ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)'s freeze message, reused.)
- *"`FetchOutcome` is an owning choice (owned payload `response` of case `Fetched`); it cannot be boxed / is not sendable / does not satisfy `new()`."* — each property-keyed rejection naming the payload that decides the classification.
- *"Case arm does not cover `Failed`: its slot pattern `>= 500` is refutable; static exhaustiveness counts only irrefutable-slot arms."* ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)'s one-level rule, made legible.)
- The must-use warning at an owning-match binding's implicit drop names the binding and the arm-position remedies.

<a id="sec-choice-exhaustiveness"></a>
### 35.6 Exhaustiveness

The static-proof rule for choice scrutinees is [§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)'s choice bullet: coverage is counted **per case name, one level deep** — a payload-free case by a constant-style pattern naming it (directly or in a `|` list), a payload case by a destructuring whose every slot is irrefutable. Guarded arms and refutable-slot arms contribute nothing to the static proof. Because the case set is closed by the declaration, exhaustiveness holds across module boundaries, and adding a case to a published choice is a source-breaking change for consumers exactly as adding a sealed leaf is.

Generic choices need no per-instantiation machinery: for `case r of Ok(var v) => …, Error(var e) => … end` over a `Result<int, ParseError>` scrutinee, coverage is by case *name* — the bindings simply take the substituted payload types. Class-hierarchy sums put the discriminant in the runtime *type*, which is why generic-leaf coverage over a closed hierarchy is not statically proven and requires an irrefutable arm ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness-generic-leaves); the v0.196 determination rule that once computed it is retired, v0.245); a choice's discriminant is a name, and the problem does not arise — for a value-shaped generic sum a choice is the steered spelling, and none of §19.6's generic-hierarchy limitation applies to it. Nested refutable patterns (`Ok(0)`) are admitted syntactically and contribute nothing statically; a program wanting nested totality writes nested `case` constructs, which are proven exhaustive level by level.

<a id="sec-choice-equality"></a>
### 35.7 Equality, hashing, `ToString`

A **value-like** choice is **auto-hashable** ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties), the [§9.2](#sec-body-records) property) when every payload field of every case is a [§9.2](#sec-body-records) admissible component type, with one addition to the recursive rule: another auto-hashable choice is admissible. The generated `=` is true exactly when both operands have the same active case and every corresponding payload compares equal by its type's `=`; the generated `GetHashCode` combines the case discriminant with the per-payload hashes (order-sensitive, [§8.3](#sec-equals-and-gethashcode)); the generated `ToString` produces `"TypeName.CaseName(field1: value1, …)"`, and `"TypeName.CaseName"` for a payload-free case. Methods, computed properties, statics, and non-equality operators neither qualify nor disqualify, per §9.2's membership list. A payload field marked **`equality skip`** ([§9.2](#sec-equality-skip); grammar A.3 `CaseField`) is excluded from its case's payload comparison and hash, and an inadmissible payload so marked does not force the use-site error **provided the choice remains value-like ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification))** — the clause never changes classification: an `owned` or class-typed payload keeps its [§35.4](#sec-choice-classification) classification, and such a choice is non-auto-hashable whatever the clause says (next paragraph). The reuse is therefore one gate stricter than the record's: a record has no value-like gate, so a skipped class-typed field can leave a borrow-bearing record hashable ([§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)); a skipped class-typed payload never rescues a choice. The clause is not admitted on a choice *case* (the case is the discriminant — skipping it is incoherent; a compile error, [§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)).

A choice that is **not** auto-hashable — any borrow-bearing or owning choice (class-typed payloads are outside the admissible-component rule, exactly as class-typed record fields are), and any value-like choice with an inadmissible payload — draws [§9.2](#sec-body-records)'s **use-site compile error** on `=`, `<>`, and direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls, unless the author declares the operators under [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)'s co-declaration rule. Declaring the choice is fine; comparing it is the error, with the same remedies §9.2 names. *(This follows the record precedent, not [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)'s inline-array borrowing-equality precedent: reference equality smuggled inside a value type's `=` is virtually never the intended semantics — rationale [§9.6](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-choices-why-a-new-kind).)*

Value-like auto-hashable choices are **hashable** and usable as hash-container keys; the other classifications are not ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)'s hashable row, unchanged).

<a id="sec-choice-boxing"></a>
### 35.8 Boxing and interfaces

Boxing follows the classification, each arm riding an existing [§8.6](#sec-boxing) rule:

- **Value-like** choices box per the general rule; the box is runtime-managed.
- **Borrow-bearing** choices box under §8.6's borrow-bearing-record rules verbatim: the boxed copy carries the same borrows, extends no lifetime, and may not escape the sources' scopes.
- **Owning** choices **cannot be boxed** — §8.6's move-only rule, word for word: boxing copies, move-only forbids copying. A program that needs an owning choice's contents to cross a boxed-value boundary transfers the payloads out through a consuming match first.

A choice may declare interface conformance (interfaces only, as for records — [§9.6](#sec-records-and-inheritance)), providing matching public members per [§10.5](#sec-restrictions)'s enum model; [§14.2](#sec-constraints)'s conformance rule gains the corresponding choice clause. For an **owning-classified** choice the conformance declaration remains legal — constraint satisfaction and generic dispatch work without boxing — but the *conversion* of an owning value to an interface or `Object` type is rejected at the conversion site (it is a boxing, forbidden above). For a generic choice this is per-instantiation ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2): a conformance-declaring choice converts at value-like instantiations and rejects at owning ones.

`Dispose` stays off the surface everywhere: choices do not implement `IDisposable` ([§8.7](#sec-dispose-is-not-on-object)) — an owning choice's disposal obligation is discharged by its *holder* (scope end, owning field, consuming match), never by calling `Dispose()` on it, exactly as for owning inline arrays.

<a id="sec-choice-nullable"></a>
### 35.9 Nullable `C?`

`C?` is the ordinary nullable value type ([§7.2](#sec-nullable-value-types)): a `C?` scrutinee adds [§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)'s explicit-`null`-arm requirement on top of the choice clause; `?.`/`??`/narrowing compose as for any nullable; boxing strips the wrapper per [§8.6](#sec-boxing)'s nullable-value-type rule (for the boxable classifications).

For an **owning** `C`, the wrapper `C?` is itself move-only (it contains a move-only value), with two consequences: `null` assignment into an owned-state `C?` location is drop-on-overwrite — the displaced value's payloads are disposed ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) — and `default(C?)` is a valid null move-only value, on the precedent of [§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)'s owning-inline-array form. The polymorphic-null-state row of [§28.3](#sec-producers)'s producers table applies to `var x: C? := null;` unchanged.

<a id="sec-choice-default-with"></a>
### 35.10 `default`, `with`, and the small surface

- **`default(C)` is a compile error for every choice type** ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)). A sum has no principled zero: electing the first-declared case would make program meaning depend on declaration order, and restricting eligibility to first-case-payload-free would make *eligibility* order-dependent, which is worse. The enum precedent (underlying-0 with a warning) does not transfer — an enum value *is* its integer ([§10.3](#sec-underlying-type)) and 0 exists whether or not named; a choice value is a case, and no case is distinguished. Consequences: choices never satisfy `where T: new()`'s value-type arm ([§14.2](#sec-constraints) keys it on `default`); `serialized skip` on a choice-typed component requires the nullable form ([§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)'s skip rule reaches this by itself). Programs wanting an empty state declare a payload-free case and construct it explicitly, or use `C?`.
- **`with` does not apply to choices.** [§9.5](#sec-non-destructive-update-with) requires a record-typed source; a choice's payloads are not independently replaceable storage (replacing one field of `Failed` is constructing a new `Failed`). A `with` over a choice-typed source is a compile error naming the remedy (construct the case anew).
- `nameof(FetchOutcome.Failed)` yields `"Failed"` ([§17.9](#sec-the-nameof-operator)); `typeof(FetchOutcome)` is ordinary; `is`/`as` over choice types follow value-type rules ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators)) and are rarely useful — the static type is always exact, choices being sealed.
- The discard `_ := c;` on an owning-choice value follows [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)'s move-only discard clause verbatim (disposes at end of statement).

<a id="sec-choice-generics"></a>
### 35.11 Generics

A choice may declare type parameters and constraints, as records do; payload fields may use the parameters. Classification is evaluated **per instantiation** under [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2, with the payload marker's meaning fixed by [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s per-instantiation erasure: a choice with `Ok(owned value: T)` is value-like at `T = int` (marker erased, payload an admissible value) and owning at `T = Connection` (marker means owned). An *unmarked* bare-type-parameter payload is classification-neutral at value and runtime-managed substitutions and **borrow-carrying** at class and interface substitutions — the same reading as a concrete unmarked class payload, making the marked/unmarked split uniform at every level of genericity: unmarked class payload = borrow (borrow-bearing choice), marked = owned (owning choice).

Method bodies of a generic choice type-check once, against `this`-as-borrow ([§35.2](#sec-choice-members)), so their checking is classification-independent; classification-dependent *admissibility* rules — boxing conversions, sendability, equality, conformance conversion — are enforced at the instantiation or use site with [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2's diagnostics. (The compiler-provided members of stdlib `Result<T, E>` are outside this check-once discipline — their bodies exist only where the members are admissible; [§35.2](#sec-choice-members)'s `this`-as-borrow rule is unchanged for them.)

The choice classification's per-instantiation *behavior* consequences (copy vs. move on assignment; disposal vs. none at scope end) fall under [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)'s behavior-dispatch reservation as its second scoped exception: the dispatch is performed by the language on a language construct — derived from structure, identical for every user, with no user-programmable hook. Users still cannot write code conditioned on a type parameter's category.

**No variance.** Variance attaches to interface and function-type parameters only ([§12.9](#sec-variance), [§14.3](#sec-generics-variance)); choices, like records and classes, are invariant. A `Result<Derived, E>` is not a `Result<Base, E>`; the conversion is an explicit re-wrap by match.

<a id="sec-choice-sendability"></a>
### 35.12 Sendability

A choice is **sendable** ([§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)) iff it is value-like and every payload field's type is sendable — the §30.14 value-type rule ("not borrow-bearing and not move-only") with the per-field transitivity the classification computation already supplies; a sendable choice crosses as a copy. Borrow-bearing choices are never sendable (they carry origin-domain borrows). **Owning choices are not directly sendable** — the §30.14 move-only exclusion, unchanged — but §30.14's transfer-closure rule 2 admits an owning-choice-typed field whose every `owned` payload class is itself a sendable class type as a field of a transfer-closed class; such a value crosses inside its owner's ownership tree, exactly as owning-inline-array fields do.

<a id="sec-choice-ffi"></a>
### 35.13 FFI and serialization

Choices are **not FFI-compatible** ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)): the honest C spelling of a sum — a tag plus a union, with the tag discipline by convention — carries real ABI questions (union layout, tag width, niche packing), and [§32.13](#sec-c-compatible-records)'s layout-promise machinery is the future home if demand materializes. The in-memory layout of a choice (tag and payload representation, niche packing) is implementation-defined; only the value-type semantics of this section are normative.

Serialization synthesis for value-like choices — the `$case`-discriminated object form — is specified in [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis).

---

<a id="sec-appendix-a"></a>
## Appendix A: Grammar

This appendix gives an EBNF grammar for Bezel. The grammar is a guide to the language's syntax; it is not strictly LL or LR. Terminal symbols are quoted; nonterminals are written `LikeThis`. `?` denotes optional, `*` denotes zero-or-more, `+` denotes one-or-more, `|` denotes alternation, parentheses group.

Whitespace and comments are recognized by the lexer and may appear between any two tokens; they are not shown in the grammar.

<a id="sec-lexical"></a>
### A.1 Lexical

```
Identifier      ::= Letter IdentCont* | "_" IdentCont+
                              /* The bare single-character `_` is NOT an
                                 Identifier: it is lexed as its own reserved
                                 token — the discard (§1.3, §17.13, B.1) — and
                                 no Identifier production ever matches it.
                                 Identifiers may begin with or contain `_`
                                 (`_camelCase`, `_f`, `snake_case`); only the
                                 bare token is reserved. */
IdentStart      ::= Letter | "_"
IdentCont       ::= IdentStart | Digit
Letter          ::= /any Unicode letter/
Digit           ::= "0".."9"
HexDigit        ::= Digit | "a".."f" | "A".."F"

IntLiteral      ::= DecLiteral | HexLiteral | BinLiteral
DecLiteral      ::= Digit ("_"* Digit)* IntSuffix?
HexLiteral      ::= "0x" HexDigit ("_"* HexDigit)* IntSuffix?
BinLiteral      ::= "0b" ("0" | "1") ("_"* ("0" | "1"))* IntSuffix?
IntSuffix       ::= "L" | "U" | "UL" | "LU"   /* case-insensitive */

FloatLiteral    ::= DigitGroup "." DigitGroup Exponent? FloatSuffix?
                  | DigitGroup Exponent FloatSuffix?
                  | DigitGroup FloatSuffix
DigitGroup      ::= Digit ("_"* Digit)*
Exponent        ::= ("e" | "E") ("+" | "-")? DigitGroup
FloatSuffix     ::= "f" | "F" | "m" | "M"     /* m -> decimal */

CharLiteral     ::= "'" CharContent "'"
StringLiteral   ::= '"' StringContent* '"'
                  | '@"' VerbatimContent* '"'
InterpString    ::= '$"' (InterpPart | StringContent)* '"'
                  | '$@"' (InterpPart | VerbatimContent)* '"'
InterpPart      ::= "{" Expression ("," "-"? IntLiteral)? (":" FormatSpec)? "}"
```

`CharContent`, `StringContent`, `VerbatimContent`, and `FormatSpec` are not given productions; their content is described in [§18.3](#sec-character-literals), [§18.4](#sec-string-literals), [§18.5](#sec-interpolated-strings), [§18.6](#sec-verbatim-strings), and [§18.8](#sec-escape-sequences-non-verbatim) of the main text. Briefly: `CharContent` is one Unicode scalar value or one escape sequence; `StringContent` is any sequence of code points or escapes other than an unescaped `"` (inside an `InterpString`, `{{` and `}}` denote literal braces, a single `{` begins an `InterpPart`, and a single unescaped `}` that does not close a hole is a compile error); `VerbatimContent` is any sequence of code points other than `"`, with `""` denoting a single `"`; `FormatSpec` is a brace-free sequence of format characters, terminated by the hole's closing `}`, with the §18.5 top-level delimitation rule deciding where it begins. Its vocabulary and semantics are normative in stdlib §2.18.

<a id="sec-source-file"></a>
### A.2 Source file

```
SourceFile      ::= ModuleDecl Import* TopDecl*
ModuleDecl      ::= "module" QualifiedName ";"
Import          ::= "import" QualifiedName ("as" Identifier)? ";"
                              /* alias: a file-scoped qualifier for the
                                 imported module (§2.2). */
QualifiedName   ::= Identifier ("." Identifier)*

TopDecl         ::= ClassDecl | InterfaceDecl | RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                  | ChoiceDecl
                  | ExtensionDecl | TypeAliasDecl | ExternBlock
TypeAliasDecl   ::= "type" Identifier GenericParams? ":=" Type
                              /* The alias binds with `:=`, like every other
                                 binding. No Visibility alternative: a module-level alias
                                 is always module-internal (§27.8). */
                    GenericConstraints* ";"
```

<a id="sec-type-declarations"></a>
### A.3 Type declarations

```
ClassDecl       ::= Visibility? Modifier* "class" Identifier GenericParams?
                    PrimaryCtorParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ClassBody
PolymorphicMember ::= "polymorphic" "(" PolyCase ("," PolyCase)* ","? ")" ";"
PolyCase ::= StringLiteral ":" TypeName
                              /* A `polymorphic` registry is a class-body member
                                 (at most one per class; takes no visibility).
                                 Each PolyCase maps a wire discriminator string
                                 to a permitted concrete derived type. The set is
                                 closed and explicitly registered: there is no
                                 reflective discovery of subtypes (rationale
                                 §5.18, §5.22). The discriminator must be a
                                 non-empty literal and unique within the
                                 registry; each TypeName must name a type
                                 assignable to the declaring class and itself
                                 type-driven serialization-eligible (declares
                                 ISerializable/IDeserializable). The declaring
                                 base class may be concrete (it registers its own
                                 discriminator) or abstract (no self case).
                                 `polymorphic` is a contextual word here, not a
                                 reserved keyword. A class enters serialization
                                 synthesis by declaring ISerializable/IDeserializable;
                                 the serialized shape is read from its field
                                 types (§9.8), with no class-header clause. */
                              /* The grammar admits modifier combinations the
                                 type system rejects: `static class C(args)`
                                 parses (Modifier* allows `static`,
                                 PrimaryCtorParams? is optional and present)
                                 but is rejected semantically — static classes
                                 cannot be instantiated and so cannot carry
                                 primary-ctor parameters (§11.7). */
ClassBody       ::= Member* "end" Identifier? ";"
Modifier        ::= "abstract" | "closed" | "sealed" | "static"
                              /* Modifier* permits any combination; the
                                 semantically valid combinations are described
                                 in §11.7. `closed` (closed abstract class)
                                 combines with no other class-shape modifier:
                                 `closed abstract`, `closed sealed`, and
                                 `closed static` are rejected, as is the
                                 pre-v0.242 spelling `sealed abstract` (the
                                 diagnostic names `closed`); other combinations
                                 with `static` are rejected. */
PrimaryCtorParams ::= "(" ParamList? ")"
Inheritance     ::= ":" InheritItem ("," InheritItem)* ","?
InheritItem     ::= Type ("(" ArgList? ")")?
                              /* The grammar accepts the optional argument list
                                 on every InheritItem; semantically, the
                                 argument list is permitted only on the base
                                 class (the first item), not on interfaces. */

InterfaceDecl   ::= Visibility? "interface" Identifier GenericParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    InterfaceMember* "end" Identifier? ";"

RecordDecl      ::= Visibility? "record" Identifier GenericParams?
                    PositionalFields?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ( ";" | RecordBody )
PositionalFields ::= "(" PositionalField ("," PositionalField)* ","? ")"
PositionalField ::= Identifier ":" Type SerializedClause? EqualityClause?
EqualityClause  ::= "equality" "skip"
                              /* Per-member exclusion from auto-equality
                                 (§9.2 "The `equality skip` clause"),
                                 mirroring SerializedClause: the marked
                                 storage component is removed from the
                                 §9.2 membership computation and cannot
                                 disqualify the record. `equality` is
                                 contextual (B.2), and within the clause
                                 `skip` is likewise contextual; only the
                                 skip form exists (no rename, no optional).
                                 Attached at PositionalField, the
                                 auto-property alternative of PropertyDecl
                                 (A.4), FieldDecl (A.4), and CaseField —
                                 in the fixed order SerializedClause?
                                 EqualityClause? where both slots exist
                                 (an arbitrary but stated order, keeping
                                 the grammar LL; each clause at most once).
                                 NOT on EnumConstant (an enum value is not
                                 a component) and NOT on ChoiceCase (the
                                 case is the discriminant); on computed
                                 properties, methods, and statics the
                                 clause is a compile error (§9.2's
                                 inert-annotation rule). */
SerializedClause ::= "serialized" ( "skip" | SerializedName )
SerializedName   ::= StringLiteral? "optional"?   /* at least one of the two
                                                     must be present */
                              /* Compiler-recognized field-name customization
                                 for serialization synthesis (§9.8). NOT an
                                 attribute system: a closed vocabulary, no
                                 user extensibility, no runtime introspection.
                                 `serialized "name"` renames; `serialized
                                 optional` makes the field tolerant
                                 (omit-if-null on write, default-if-missing on
                                 read); `serialized "name" optional` combines
                                 the two; `serialized skip` excludes the field
                                 and is mutually exclusive with a name or
                                 `optional`. `skip` and `optional` are
                                 contextual words here, not reserved keywords;
                                 the `SerializedName` form requires at least
                                 one of the string or `optional` (a bare
                                 `serialized` is a syntax error). */
RecordBody      ::= Member* "end" Identifier? ";"

EnumDecl        ::= Visibility? "enum" Identifier EnumInheritance?
                    EnumConstants
                    EnumMember* "end" Identifier? ";"
EnumInheritance ::= ":" IntegerType ("," InheritItem)* ","?
                  | ":" InheritItem ("," InheritItem)* ","?
                              /* The first form is `enum E: int, IComparable<E>` —
                                 explicit underlying type followed by interfaces.
                                 The second form is `enum E: IComparable<E>` —
                                 default underlying type (int), interfaces only.
                                 The grammar disambiguates by whether the first
                                 token after `:` is an IntegerType keyword. */
EnumConstants   ::= EnumConstant ("," EnumConstant)* ","? ";"
EnumConstant    ::= Identifier (":=" ConstExpr)? SerializedClause?

ChoiceDecl      ::= Visibility? "choice" Identifier GenericParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ChoiceCases
                    ChoiceMember* "end" Identifier? ";"
ChoiceCases     ::= ChoiceCase ("," ChoiceCase)* ","? ";"
ChoiceCase      ::= Identifier CasePayload? SerializedClause?
                              /* SerializedClause on a case admits the rename
                                 form only; `skip` and `optional` are rejected
                                 semantically, as on enum constants (§9.8). */
CasePayload     ::= "(" CaseField ("," CaseField)* ","? ")"
CaseField       ::= "owned"? Identifier ":" Type SerializedClause? EqualityClause?
                              /* The payload field form is PositionalField plus
                                 the optional leading `owned` marker; the
                                 marker's admissibility follows §28.1's type
                                 requirement, including the bare-type-parameter
                                 erasure. Inheritance names interfaces only
                                 (as for records). §35.1. */
ChoiceMember    ::= MethodDecl | ExpressionPropertyDecl
                  | StaticReadonlyDecl | StaticConstDecl
                  | OperatorDecl
                              /* Identical to EnumMember; kept as a named
                                 production so the two sections can restrict
                                 independently if they ever diverge. */
                              /* `serialized "name"` on an enum constant
                                 customizes that member's serialized name
                                 (§9.8). `serialized skip` and `serialized
                                 optional` are not admitted on enum constants
                                 — an enum value is a single member, not a
                                 field that can be omitted or defaulted; using
                                 them here is a compile error. */

ExtensionDecl   ::= Visibility? "extension" Type GenericConstraints*
                    ExtensionMember* "end" "extension"? ";"

ExternBlock     ::= "extern" StringLiteral ("convention" StringLiteral)?
                    ExternDecl+ "end" "extern"? ";"
ExternDecl      ::= Visibility? "method" Identifier "(" ExternParamList? ")"
                    (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    (":=" "symbol" StringLiteral VariadicClause?)? ";"
ExternParamList ::= ExternParam ("," ExternParam)* ","?
ExternParam     ::= Param | "env"
VariadicClause  ::= "variadic" "(" IntLiteral ")"
                              /* `owned` on the return marks ownership transfer
                                 per §32.6's contract (§28.1: owned returns are
                                 declared). `symbol`, `variadic`, and `env` are
                                 contextual (Appendix B.2). In ExternParam the
                                 parser distinguishes by two-token lookahead:
                                 `env` followed by `:` is an ordinary Param
                                 named `env`; a bare `env` is the user-data
                                 slot marker (§32.8). `env` also appears as a
                                 parameter-type atom inside a function-typed
                                 extern parameter (§32.8); the type grammar
                                 admits it there as an ordinary identifier and
                                 §32.8's pairing rules give it meaning — the
                                 over-admit-and-reject-semantically pattern.
                                 Param modifiers: `ref`/`out` admitted per
                                 §32.5's boundary rules; `owned`, `out owned`,
                                 and `scoped` rejected semantically. */
```

<a id="sec-members"></a>
### A.4 Members

```
Member          ::= FieldDecl | MethodDecl | PropertyDecl | IndexerDecl
                  | ConstructorDecl | DestructorDecl
                  | OperatorDecl | NestedTypeDecl | ConstDecl
                  | PolymorphicMember | InvariantDecl
ExtensionMember ::= MethodDecl | ExpressionPropertyDecl
                              /* `static` is rejected inside extension blocks
                                 (§26.3); MethodDecl's "static"?
                                 alternative does not apply here. */

InterfaceMember ::= IfaceMethod | IfaceProperty | IfaceIndexer
                  | IfaceStaticMethod | IfaceStaticOperator
IfaceStaticMethod   ::= "static" "pure"? "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                        "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                        ContractClause* ";"
                              /* same body slot as IfaceMethod (§22.16) */
IfaceStaticOperator ::= "static" "operator" OpToken
                        "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)? ";"
                              /* §11.8: abstract-only — a body is an
                                 error; static properties/consts are
                                 deferred. Conformance and dispatch rules in
                                 §11.8. */
IfaceMethod     ::= "pure"? "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                    "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    ContractClause* ";"
                              /* clauses are self-delimited; the lone ";" is the
                                 uniform member terminator, clause-bearing or not
                                 (§22.16) */
                              /* `owned` on the return type follows the same
                                 rule as in MethodDecl. An interface declaring
                                 an `owned` return requires implementations to
                                 declare an `owned` return (§11.2's exact-match
                                 rule). */
IfaceProperty   ::= "pure"? "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type
                    ( ";" | Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";" )
IfaceIndexer    ::= "pure"? "readonly"? "property" "[" ParamList "]" ":" Type
                    ( ";" | Accessor* "end" ";" )
                              /* The accessor-block form declares explicit get/set
                                 accessors (e.g. `get; set(owned);`) on an interface
                                 property or indexer; in interface context each
                                 Accessor uses the `;`-terminated AccessorBody (no
                                 implementation), enforced semantically. See §23.3. */
FieldDecl       ::= Visibility "static"? ("owned" | "scoped")? "readonly"?
                    EqualityClause? Identifier ":" Type (":=" Expression)? ";"
                              /* "scoped" fields (§28.14) hold storage-
                                 bounded callbacks: function-typed only,
                                 invocable/overwritable/clearable, never read
                                 out as an escaping value. */
                              /* EqualityClause here is the point of §9.2's
                                 clause: an explicit field is §9.2's
                                 disqualifier, and the clause is what
                                 un-disqualifies it (record bodies; on a
                                 class field, and on a static field
                                 anywhere, it is rejected semantically —
                                 §9.2). SerializedClause never appears on
                                 FieldDecl: explicit fields are not
                                 serialized components of a record
                                 (§9.8). */
ConstDecl       ::= Visibility "static"? "const" Identifier (":" Type)?
                    ":=" ConstExpr ";"

ContractClause  ::= "static"? ("requires" | "ensures") "(" Expression ")"
                              /* the parentheses are clause syntax, not expression
                                 tokens (§22.16): a clause is self-
                                 delimiting and carries no terminator. */
InvariantDecl   ::= "static"? "invariant" "(" Expression ")" ";"
                              /* class bodies only; rejected semantically in
                                 records and static classes (§22.16); the `;` is
                                 the ordinary member terminator. */
                              /* the clause region (§22.16): after the signature's
                                 GenericConstraints*, the tokens requires/ensures
                                 (or static followed by either) open it; keyword
                                 reading always wins there (the B.2 env rule). */

MethodDecl      ::= Visibility "static"? ("async" | "pure")? VirtualKind?
                    "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                    "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    GenericConstraints* ContractClause*
                    MethodBody
                              /* clauses are self-delimited (§22.16); every
                                 MethodBody alternative, the lone ";" included, is
                                 reachable at any clause count */
                              /* The optional `owned` modifier on the return
                                 type marks methods whose result transfers
                                 ownership to the caller (§28.8). It applies
                                 to class-typed returns; for non-class types
                                 it is rejected semantically. */
VirtualKind     ::= "abstract" | "virtual" | "sealed"? "override"
MethodBody      ::= "=>" (Expression | AssignmentStmt) ";"
                              /* The AssignmentStmt alternative is
                                 valid only on methods with no declared return
                                 type (unit result); it makes the accessor
                                 shape `set => _x := value;` available to the
                                 identically-shaped unit method:
                                 `method SetX(v: int) => _x := v;` (§22.2).
                                 Enforced semantically. */
                  | Statement* "end" Identifier? ";"
                  | ";"                /* body-less method: requires
                                          VirtualKind = "abstract"; enforced
                                          semantically. Interface methods use
                                          IfaceMethod, not MethodDecl, so the
                                          ";" body here is exclusively for
                                          abstract members. */

PropertyDecl    ::= Visibility "static"? "pure"? VirtualKind?
                    "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type
                    PropertyBody
PropertyBody    ::= "=>" Expression ";"
                  | AutoAccessorVis? (":=" Expression)? SerializedClause? EqualityClause? ";"   /* auto-property */
                              /* the two clauses in the fixed order shown,
                                 each at most once (A.3 EqualityClause). */
                  | Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";"
AutoAccessorVis ::= Visibility ("get" | "set")   /* e.g. `private set` */
Accessor        ::= Visibility? "pure"? "get" AccessorBody
                  | Visibility? "set" SetterParamSpec? AccessorBody
                              /* "pure" is admitted on "get" only — a "pure set"
                                 does not parse (the set alternative carries no
                                 "pure" slot); §22.15 states the rule */
SetterParamSpec ::= "(" ParamMod? Identifier? ")"
                              /* Explicit setter parameter spec, used when
                                 the parameter modifier needs to be declared
                                 (typically `owned` for owned-element-collection
                                 indexer setters). The parameter's type is
                                 always the property's declared type, so it
                                 is not repeated here. When the parameter
                                 name is omitted (only the modifier given,
                                 as in `set(owned)`), the implicit name
                                 remains `value`. When the SetterParamSpec
                                 is omitted entirely (`set` alone), the
                                 implicit `value` parameter has no modifier
                                 and takes a borrow of the property's declared
                                 type (§22.3, §23.3). */
ParamMod        ::= "owned"
                              /* Only `owned` is meaningful on a setter's value
                                 parameter: the parameter is an input,
                                 so `ref`/`out` do not parse here. */
AccessorBody    ::= "=>" (Expression | AssignmentStmt | "do" Statement* "end") ";"
                  | ";"                                  /* abstract / interface body */
                              /* The single-statement form `set => _x := value;`
                                 (an AssignmentStmt) parallels the §13.6 prose; it
                                 is distinct from the expression form (assignment is
                                 a statement, not an expression) and the do-block
                                 form. */

IndexerDecl     ::= Visibility "static"? "pure"? VirtualKind?
                              /* "static" is over-admitted here and rejected
                                 semantically: indexers may not be static
                                 (§23.5). Parameter default values (":=" in
                                 the shared ParamList) are likewise
                                 over-admitted and rejected: indexer
                                 parameters may not declare defaults
                                 (§23.5). */
                    "readonly"? "property" "[" ParamList "]" ":" Type
                    PropertyBody
                              /* IndexerDecl reuses PropertyBody, whose block
                                 form is `Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";"`.
```
