```
                                 The optional Identifier is for property
                                 declarations (matching the property's name);
                                 indexers have no name, so the only valid
                                 form for an indexer's block-form `end` is
                                 plain `end;`. Enforced semantically —
                                 IfaceIndexer states the same rule structurally
                                 in its bespoke body; this production's
                                 reuse-plus-semantic-rejection is the grammar's
                                 deliberate shared-production policy. */

ConstructorDecl ::= Visibility "pure"? "constructor" "(" ParamList? ")"
                    ContractClause*
                              /* the static-constructor alternative admits no
                                 "pure" (§22.15) and no clauses (§22.16) */
                    CtorChain? Statement* "end" "constructor"? ";"
                  | "static" "constructor" "(" ")"
                    Statement* "end" "constructor"? ";"
CtorChain       ::= ("base" | "this") "(" ArgList? ")" ";"

DestructorDecl  ::= "destructor" Statement* "end" "destructor"? ";"

OperatorDecl    ::= "public" "static" "pure"? "method" "operator" OpToken
                    "(" ParamList ")" ":" "owned"? Type OperatorBody
                              /* `owned` on an operator's return type is
                                 permitted for class-typed operators that
                                 allocate. Most operator overloads return
                                 records or value types and do not need it.
                                 ParamList is the shared production; parameter
                                 modifiers on operator parameters are rejected
                                 semantically (§25.2). */
OperatorBody    ::= "=>" Expression ";"
                  | Statement* "end" ("operator" OpToken)? ";"
OpToken         ::= "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "mod" | "&" | "|" | "^"
                  | "<<" | ">>" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">="
                  | "=" | "<>" | "~" | "++" | "--"

NestedTypeDecl  ::= ClassDecl | InterfaceDecl | RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                              /* The reused productions carry `Visibility?` for
                                 the top-level default-internal rule (§13.2).
                                 In nested position the visibility keyword is
                                 required (§13.3, §11.6); omission is
                                 rejected semantically. */

ParamList       ::= Param ("," Param)* ","?
Param           ::= ParamModifiers? Identifier ":" Type (":=" Expression)?
                    OutNullPostcond?
                              /* A method/constructor parameter cannot be named
                                 `_` — the bare token is not an Identifier
                                 (A.1), and the rejection diagnostic says why:
                                 parameter names are call-site-addressable API
                                 surface (§22.5, §2.8.2); choose a name
                                 (§17.13). Lambda parameters differ: LambdaParam
                                 (A.7) admits the bare-`_` ignore. */
                              /* `owned` precedes the identifier in every
                                 named-declaration position — Param, LambdaParam
                                 (via FuncParamMods, A.7), FieldDecl,
                                 CaseField, StaticReadonlyDecl; the post-colon
                                 spelling `x: owned T` does not parse (§28.1:
                                 the modifier attaches to the declaration, not
                                 the type). The pre-Type spelling ("owned"?
                                 Type) exists only in positions with no
                                 identifier — return types and FunctionType
                                 slots. */
OutNullPostcond ::= "when" ("true" | "false")
                              /* (§22.4): admitted only on `out` /
                                 `out owned` parameters of nullable type in
                                 bool-returning methods — a checked non-null
                                 postcondition tied to the stated result. No
                                 parse ambiguity: out parameters never carry
                                 defaults (§22.5), so the clause always
                                 directly follows the Type. */
ParamModifiers  ::= "ref"
                  | "out" "owned"?
                  | "owned"
                  | "scoped"
                              /* "scoped" is valid on function-typed
                                 parameters (§28.14: storage-bounded
                                 callback capture) and on class/interface-typed
                                 parameters (§28.14: storage-
                                 bounded borrow — scoped construction). On a
                                 static method it requires an `owned` return
                                 (§28.14). Other parameter types are
                                 rejected semantically. Illegal on extern
                                 declarations (§32). */
ArgList         ::= Argument ("," Argument)* ","?
Argument        ::= ArgModifiers ArgExpression
                  | (Identifier ":=")? ArgExpression
                              /* ref/out arguments and move-rooted arguments
                                 are positional-only (§22.5): the named form
                                 is for plain values. The operand category
                                 for ref/out arguments is semantic: §22.3
                                 "ref and out argument locations". Named
                                 arguments are additionally rejected at the
                                 index position (§23.5) — admitted by the
                                 shared grammar, rejected semantically. */
ArgModifiers    ::= "ref"
                  | "out" "var"?
                  | "out" "using" "var"
                  | "out" "owned" "var"
                  | "scoped"
                              /* The bare "owned" alternative was deleted at
                                 v0.246 (proposal 0090): the call-site transfer
                                 marker is part of the argument EXPRESSION —
                                 `M(move x)` parses through the plain
                                 ArgExpression path as an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr (A.7; §22.3, §28.8.1). "out owned var"
                                 stays: it declares a fresh owned binding at
                                 the call site — a declaration position
                                 (§22.4), on `owned`'s declarative side of the
                                 line. "scoped" (§22.3/§28.14) marks a
                                 class/interface-typed borrow argument to a
                                 `scoped` parameter — `M(scoped x)`; fresh
                                 producers rejected (§9.7). `scoped` remains an
                                 argument modifier: it marks a lending mode,
                                 not an action — the asymmetry with `move` is
                                 deliberate (§22.3). */
ArgExpression   ::= Expression | "_"
                              /* The "_" alternative is admitted by the grammar
                                 in any argument position and is the ONLY
                                 reading of `_` there — no Expression contains
                                 the bare token (A.1). It is semantically valid
                                 only when the corresponding parameter is `out`
                                 and the caller chooses to ignore the produced
                                 value (§22.4); in every non-out position —
                                 `ref _` included — it is a compile error
                                 (§17.13: a `ref` argument reads its operand,
                                 which a discard cannot supply). */

EnumMember      ::= MethodDecl | ExpressionPropertyDecl
                  | StaticReadonlyDecl | StaticConstDecl
                  | OperatorDecl
                              /* enums may overload operators
                                 (§25, §10.4). OperatorDecl is `public static`
                                 only, as everywhere. */
ExpressionPropertyDecl ::= Visibility "pure"? "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type "=>" Expression ";"
                  /* "readonly" is redundant on expression-bodied properties (no setter exists);
                     it is permitted for consistency with block-form property syntax. */
StaticReadonlyDecl     ::= Visibility "static" "owned"? "readonly" Identifier ":" Type ":=" Expression ";"
                  /* "owned": a static owned readonly field on an enum
                     participates in §22.13's program-exit disposal exactly as on
                     a class; modifier order per §11.5. */
StaticConstDecl        ::= Visibility "const" Identifier (":" Type)? ":=" ConstExpr ";"

Visibility      ::= "public" | "internal" | "protected" | "private"

GenericParams   ::= "<" GenericParam ("," GenericParam)* ","? ">"
GenericParam    ::= Variance? Identifier
Variance        ::= "in" | "out"
                              /* Variance markers are semantically valid only on
                                 interface type parameters (§12.9; and not
                                 on interfaces declaring static members, §11.8).
                                 On class/record/method/alias parameters the
                                 marker is rejected semantically. */
GenericConstraints ::= "where" Identifier ":" Constraint ("," Constraint)* ","?
                              /* The former `where T is owned` modifier-
                                 constraint form is retired along with `<owned T>`
                                 generic arguments (§14.4); constraints bound
                                 types only. */
Constraint      ::= "class" | "value" | "notnull" | "sendable" | "hashable" | "new" "(" ")" | Type
                              /* "new" "(" ")" is the parameterless-constructor
                                 constraint, three tokens with whitespace
                                 permitted (lexer-level) — `new()` and
                                 `new ()` are equivalent. */
```

<a id="sec-types"></a>
### A.5 Types

```
Type            ::= TypeNoNullable "?"?
TypeNoNullable  ::= QualifiedName GenericArgs?
                  | PrimitiveType
                  | InlineArrayType
                  | FunctionType
                  | "(" FunctionType ")"       /* parenthesized function type,
                                                  required before the `?`
                                                  nullable marker (§27.2):
                                                  `((int) -> bool)?`. In `-> T?`
                                                  the `?` binds to the return
                                                  type, not the function type. */
                  | "(" ")"                    /* unit type */
InlineArrayType ::= "[" ConstIntExpr "owned"? "]" Type
                              /* Inline array. Size must be a compile-time
                                 integer constant > 0. The optional `owned`
                                 marker (between size and closing bracket)
                                 marks slot ownership; the array becomes
                                 a move-only value type. See §15.1, §15.3.
                                 The inner Type is parsed greedily — `[3]int?`
                                 means an inline array of nullable int, not
                                 a nullable inline array. Nullable inline-array
                                 types are not provided in this revision. */
ConstIntExpr    ::= Expression           /* a §17.14 constant expression of
                       integer type; see §15.1 "Size" */
GenericArgs     ::= "<" GenericArg ("," GenericArg)* ","? ">"
GenericArg      ::= Type
                              /* `owned` is not admitted on
                                 generic type arguments; the owned-bearing
                                 collection and task types are separate named
                                 classes (`OwningArray<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, etc.).
                                 See §14.4. */
FunctionType    ::= "(" (FuncParamType ("," FuncParamType)* ","?)? ")" "->" "owned"? Type
                              /* The optional `owned` on the return marks
                                 a function type whose result transfers
                                 ownership to the caller. See §28.1. The
                                 `owned` is part of the function type's
                                 identity: `() -> Connection` and
                                 `() -> owned Connection` are distinct types. */
FuncParamType   ::= FuncParamMods? (Identifier ":")? Type
FuncParamMods   ::= "ref" | "scoped"
                  | "out" "owned"?
                  | "owned"
                              /* Same set as the method-declaration ParamModifiers
                                 (§A.4); function types and method declarations
                                 share modifier syntax exactly. The `out owned`
                                 combination represents an out-parameter that
                                 produces an owned value. */
IntegerType     ::= "byte" | "sbyte" | "short" | "ushort"
                  | "int" | "uint" | "long" | "ulong"
PrimitiveType   ::= IntegerType | "float" | "double" | "decimal"
                  | "bool" | "char" | "string"
                              /* The primitive KEYWORD spellings are tokens, not
                                 identifiers (§1.4, §3.4), so `var x: int` and
                                 `int.Parse(s)` need this production; the
                                 PascalCase aliases (`Int32`, `String`, …) arrive
                                 through QualifiedName as ordinary identifiers. */
```

<a id="sec-appendix-a-statements"></a>
### A.6 Statements

```
Statement       ::= LocalDecl | LocalConstDecl | AssignmentStmt | ExpressionStmt
                  | DiscardStmt
                  | IfStmt | WhileStmt | ForStmt | DoEndBlock
                  | CaseStmt | WhenStmt
                  | ReturnStmt | ThrowStmt | BreakStmt | ContinueStmt
                  | TryStmt | YieldStmt
                  | IncrementStmt
                  | LocalTypeDecl

LocalTypeDecl   ::= RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                              /* Method-local type declaration (§21.10):
                                 `record`/`enum` are reserved and begin no other
                                 statement — token-one commit, no existing program
                                 changes meaning. The reused A.3 productions are
                                 restricted semantically: the Visibility? slot must
                                 be empty (a local type has no access surface —
                                 contrast §11.6, where nested types REQUIRE the
                                 keyword) and the GenericParams? slot must be empty
                                 (v1). Scope: the declaration to the innermost
                                 enclosing block's end, like a local variable
                                 (§21.6); order-significant (no forward references);
                                 no signature positions; no shadowing of a visible
                                 type name (§21.10). References to enclosing generic
                                 parameters are rejected (v1, §21.10). A.3
                                 (RecordDecl, EnumDecl) is unchanged. */

CaseStmt        ::= "case" Expression "of" CaseArm ("," CaseArm)* ","? "end" "case"? ";"
WhenStmt        ::= "when" WhenArm ("," WhenArm)* ","? "end" "when"? ";"
                              /* The statement forms of §19's constructs:
                                 `end`-terminated, with the statement's `;`
                                 following the closer. Arms use the same CaseArm/
                                 WhenArm grammar as the A.7 atoms, and here
                                 ArmBody additionally admits its Statement and
                                 `do … end` alternatives; an expression-bodied
                                 arm's value is discarded per §21.9, applied per
                                 arm. The former `"owned"?` scrutinee marker was
                                 deleted at v0.246 (proposal 0090): the scrutinee
                                 transfer marker is an ordinary scrutinee
                                 Expression whose root is an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr — `case move x of` — under §35.5's
                                 rules, identical to the atom's. */

LocalDecl       ::= "var" Identifier (":" Type)? (":=" Expression)? ";"
                  | "using" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                  | "await" "using" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                              /* `var _ := e;` does not parse as a LocalDecl —
                                 `_` is not an Identifier (A.1) — and is
                                 rejected with the two-remedy diagnostic:
                                 `_ := e;` (end of statement) or
                                 `using var _ := e;` (scope end) — §17.13,
                                 §21.1. The `"_"` alternative on the using-var
                                 forms is the anonymous owning binding
                                 (§17.13, §28.10): scope-end disposal, no name
                                 bound. Its `(":" Type)?` ascription slot is
                                 retained (`using var _: Stream := e;`) — the
                                 no-annotation rule governs the bare ignores,
                                 not this binding. */
                              /* The `await using var` form is admitted by the
                                 grammar at any LocalDecl position; it is
                                 valid only inside `async` methods and `async`
                                 lambdas, enforced semantically (§28.12,
                                 Appendix C.6). The binding-position
                                 transfer marker is the identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr (A.7) at RHS root: `var y := move x;`
                                 is the MoveExpr as the entire RHS; admission
                                 is positional, enforced
                                 semantically (§28.3). A
                                 LocalDecl with neither a type ascription nor an
                                 initializer is rejected semantically (nothing
                                 determines the type; typed uninitialized locals
                                 follow §7.9's assignment-before-read rules). */

LocalConstDecl  ::= "const" Identifier (":" Type)? ":=" ConstExpr ";"
                              /* Initializer classified per §21.1:
                                 a §17.14 constant expression of primitive or
                                 string type is a compile-time constant;
                                 anything else is a runtime const. ConstExpr
                                 remains Expression, restricted semantically. */
                                /* local const; no visibility or static modifier */

AssignmentStmt  ::= LValue AssignOp Expression ";"
                              /* The assignment-position transfer marker
                                 is the identifier-operand MoveExpr (A.7) at
                                 RHS root: `y := move x;`. Valid only with ":=";
                                 admission is positional, enforced semantically
                                 (§28.3). */
AssignOp        ::= ":=" | "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/=" | "mod=" | "&=" | "|="
                  | "^=" | "<<=" | ">>=" | "??="
                              /* `mod=` is one token, lexed by longest match:
                                 the keyword `mod` immediately followed by `=`
                                 with no intervening space. `x mod = y` remains
                                 a syntax error. */
LValue          ::= Identifier | "this"
                  | LValue "." Identifier
                  | LValue "[" ArgList "]"
                              /* LValues have a restricted shape: the base must
                                 be `Identifier` or `this`, and only `.field`
                                 and `[index]` accesses extend the chain.
                                 Method-call results cannot serve as the base
                                 of an assignment; `getCache().items[0] := v`
                                 does not parse. Such cases require extracting
                                 the call result into a local variable first:
                                 `var c := getCache(); c.items[0] := v;`. */

DiscardStmt     ::= "_" ":=" Expression ";"            /* explicit discard */

IncrementStmt   ::= LValue ("++" | "--") ";"
ExpressionStmt  ::= Expression ";"

IfStmt          ::= "if" Expression "then" Statement*
                    ("elif" Expression "then" Statement*)*
                    ("else" Statement*)?
                    "end" "if"? ";"
                              /* every statement-level closer
                                 may optionally repeat its introducing keyword,
                                 checked when present — one uniform end-label
                                 rule (§1.6). */

LoopLabel       ::= Identifier ":"
                              /* only loop statements take a loop label.
                                 The Identifier closer alternative below is
                                 admitted grammatically on every loop and
                                 checked per §1.6: it must equal the loop's
                                 label; on an unlabeled loop an identifier
                                 closer is rejected, and on a labeled loop the
                                 keyword closer is rejected (the construct is
                                 named). No parse ambiguity: no statement
                                 begins Identifier ":" (":=" is one lexeme), and
                                 after "Identifier :" the parser requires "for",
                                 "while", or "await" "for". */

WhileStmt       ::= LoopLabel? "while" Expression "do" Statement*
                    "end" ("while" | Identifier)? ";"

ForStmt         ::= LoopLabel? "for" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? "in" Expression
                    "do" Statement* "end" ("for" | Identifier)? ";"
                  | LoopLabel? "await" "for" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? "in" Expression
                    ("with" Expression)? "do" Statement* "end" ("for" | Identifier)? ";"
                              /* The `"_"` alternative is the loop-variable
                                 ignore (§21.4, §17.13): binds nothing. The
                                 grammar over-admits the ascription on it;
                                 `for var _: T in …` is rejected semantically —
                                 a bare ignore takes its type from context,
                                 never an annotation (§17.13). */

DoEndBlock      ::= "do" Statement* "end" "do"? ";"

ReturnStmt      ::= "return" Expression? ";"
ThrowStmt       ::= "throw" Expression? ";"
BreakStmt       ::= "break" Identifier? ";"
ContinueStmt    ::= "continue" Identifier? ";"

TryStmt         ::= "try" Statement* CatchBlock FinallyClause? "end" "try"? ";"
                  | "try" Statement* FinallyClause "end" "try"? ";"
CatchBlock      ::= "catch" CatchArm ("," CatchArm)* ","?
CatchArm        ::= CatchPattern ("when" Expression)? "=>" ArmBody
CatchPattern    ::= Type ("|" Type)*                          /* no binding */
                  | "var" Identifier ":" Type ("|" Type)*      /* binding */
                              /* Multi-type alternatives are `|`-separated
                                 — the same alternatives
                                 spelling as case patterns (AltPattern). */
FinallyClause   ::= "finally" Statement*

YieldStmt       ::= "yield" "return" Expression ";"
                  | "yield" "break" ";"
```

<a id="sec-expressions"></a>
### A.7 Expressions

The grammar shown here is informal: it lists the alternatives at each precedence level rather than expanding every binary level into recursive productions. Operator precedence is given in [§17.1](#sec-precedence).

```
Expression      ::= LogicalOr
                  | ThrowExpr
                              /* IfExpr, CaseExpr, and WhenExpr are PrimaryAtom
                                 forms (self-delimited, usable in any operand
                                 position); no conditional level exists in the
                                 operator table (§17.1). A bare ThrowExpr
                                 appears at Expression top level and, because an
                                 atom's branches and arm bodies derive full
                                 Expressions, in any branch or arm body (§20). */
ThrowExpr       ::= "throw" Expression?
                              /* Bare "throw" (no operand) is valid only inside a
                                 catch arm body; outside a catch arm body, the
                                 operand is required. Enforced semantically. */
LogicalOr       ::= LogicalAnd ("or" LogicalAnd)*
LogicalAnd      ::= NullCoalesce ("and" NullCoalesce)*
NullCoalesce    ::= Equality ("??" (ThrowExpr | NullCoalesce))?
                              /* The right operand may be a throw expression —
                                 `x ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(…)`
                                 (§17.12); ThrowExpr is bottom-typed there. */
Equality        ::= Relational (("=" | "<>") Relational)*
Relational      ::= BitwiseOr (RelTail)*
RelTail         ::= RelOp BitwiseOr
                  | TypeRel TypeOperand
RelOp           ::= "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" | "in"
TypeRel         ::= "is" "not"? | "as"
TypeOperand     ::= Type | "null"
                              /* "is", "is not", and "as" take a Type on the
                                 right so that generic type arguments parse
                                 correctly: `x is Array<int>` parses with
                                 `Array<int>` as a Type, not as the bitwise
                                 expression `Array < int >`. The `null`
                                 alternative covers `is null` and `is not null`
                                 (§17.4); `as null` is a type error caught
                                 semantically. The other relational operators
                                 (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `in`) take ordinary
                                 expressions and use RelOp. */
BitwiseOr       ::= BitwiseXor ("|" BitwiseXor)*
BitwiseXor      ::= BitwiseAnd ("^" BitwiseAnd)*
BitwiseAnd      ::= RangeExpr ("&" RangeExpr)*
RangeExpr       ::= Shift                                    /* no range */
                  | Shift (".." | "..<") Shift ("step" Shift)?
                                                             /* closed: a..b, a..<b,
                                                                with optional step */
                  | Shift ".."                               /* low-only: a..  */
                  | (".." | "..<") Shift                     /* high-only: ..b, ..<b */
                  | ".."                                     /* fully open: ..  */
                              /* Range bounds parse as Shift expressions, so
                                 `0..n+1` and `1<<2..1<<10` parse correctly,
                                 while `score in 60..100` and `r = 0..10`
                                 parse with the range as the right operand
                                 of the looser `in`/`=` operator. The open-
                                 ended forms support pattern matching (`..<0`
                                 matches values less than 0, `31..` matches
                                 values at or above 31; §19.3) and array
                                 slicing (`arr[..5]`, `arr[10..]`, `arr[..]`;
                                 §16.2). `step` is admitted only on closed
                                 ranges; open-ended ranges have no enumerable
                                 step semantics. */
Shift           ::= Additive (("<<" | ">>") Additive)*
Additive        ::= Multiplicative (("+" | "-") Multiplicative)*
Multiplicative  ::= UnaryExpr (("*" | "/" | "mod") UnaryExpr)*
                              /* The binary-level productions above derive the
                                 operator-category mixes that §17.2's mandatory-
                                 parenthesization rules reject (bitwise↔equality/
                                 relational/logical, shift↔additive, range↔bitwise);
                                 such a mix parses and is then rejected post-parse,
                                 enforced semantically per §17.2. */
UnaryExpr       ::= ("+" | "-" | "not" | "~") UnaryExpr
                  | "await" UnaryExpr
                  | PrimaryExpr
                              /* Right-recursive: `not not x`, `- -x` (with the
                                 space; `--` lexes as the decrement token), and
                                 `-(await x)` without parens all derive, matching
                                 §17.1 level 2's right-to-left associativity. */
PrimaryExpr     ::= PrimaryAtom PrimarySuffix*
PrimarySuffix   ::= "." Identifier GenericArgs?
                  | "?." Identifier GenericArgs?
                              /* The optional GenericArgs supplies explicit
                                 method type arguments at a call site:
                                 `obj.Method<int>(args)`. The GenericArgs
                                 belong to the member name; a following
                                 `"(" ArgList? ")"` suffix is the call.
                                 Same "generic arguments in an expression"
                                 family as the PrimaryAtom `Identifier
                                 GenericArgs?` form below. See §22.12. */
                  | "[" ArgList "]"
                  | "(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "?(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "!"
                  | "with" "(" InitAssign ("," InitAssign)* ","? ")"
                              /* The `with` suffix is the record copy-with-
                                 overrides expression (§9.5). It requires a
                                 record-typed source; a class-typed source is
                                 rejected semantically (§9.5) — the
                                 grammar over-admits and the type checker
                                 rejects, the same pattern A.4 uses throughout. */

PrimaryAtom     ::= Literal
                  | PrimitiveType
                              /* A primitive keyword in expression position:
                                 static access `int.Parse(s)` / `int.MaxValue`
                                 (§3.4) and the cast-call `int(d)` (§5.2). When a
                                 name in this position is followed by `?(`, the
                                 type reading wins: `T?(x)` where T resolves to a
                                 type is the §5.3 nullable cast, not a §7.6
                                 null-conditional call. */
                  | Identifier GenericArgs?
                              /* The optional GenericArgs lets a generic type
                                 name appear in receiver/expression position so
                                 its static members can be accessed with the type
                                 arguments supplied — `Registry<int>.Register()`,
                                 `Cache<string>.Default`. Without a trailing
                                 member-access (or call) suffix, a bare
                                 `Identifier GenericArgs` is not a complete
                                 expression. The `<` that opens GenericArgs here
                                 is the well-known generics-vs-less-than ambiguity;
                                 the parser admits the GenericArgs reading only
                                 when the `<…>` is balanced and followed by a
                                 token that can continue a primary expression
                                 (`.`, `?.`, `(`, `[`), otherwise `<` is the
                                 relational operator. See §22.12. */
                  | "(" Expression ")"
                  | NewExpr
                  | MoveExpr
                  | LambdaExpr
                  | IfExpr
                  | CaseExpr
                  | WhenExpr
                  | BindExpr
                  | "this" | "base"
                  | NameOfExpr | TypeOfExpr | DefaultExpr
                  | CollectionLiteral
                  | "(" ")"                             /* unit value */

MoveExpr        ::= "move" PrimaryExpr
                              /* The PrimaryExpr operand must syntactically
                                 resolve to one of: (a) a field access on a
                                 class instance — `Identifier "." Identifier`
                                 (this.f abbreviated as f) or
                                 `PrimaryExpr "." Identifier` (obj.f), where
                                 the named field is `owned`; (b) an
                                 indexer access `PrimaryExpr "[" Expression "]"`
                                 where the receiver is an owning collection
                                 admitting slot-level move (`OwningArray<T>`,
                                 `OwningDictionary<K, V>`, `OwningBuffer<T>`
                                 for class-typed T, `Span<T>` over class-typed
                                 `OwningBuffer<T>`, or an owning inline array
                                 `[N owned]…`); or (c) a bare Identifier naming
                                 a local binding or `owned` parameter — the
                                 K3.4 transfer marker (v0.246, proposal 0090;
                                 formerly the `"owned" Identifier`
                                 MarkedTransfer atom, deleted). Alternative
                                 (c)'s admission is positional, enforced
                                 semantically (§28.3): the entire RHS of a
                                 binding or assignment (a BindExpr clause's RHS
                                 included), an argument root (`M(move x)`,
                                 §22.3), positional only (§22.5), a `case`
                                 scrutinee root (§35.5), an if-expression
                                 branch, or an expression-`case`/`when` arm
                                 result. Everywhere else — `??` operands,
                                 operator operands, guards, nested
                                 subexpressions — it is a compile error naming
                                 axiom A7's narrowed bound; at an announced
                                 target (`return`/`throw` operands, the
                                 discard RHS, owned-slot stores, a Pattern B
                                 `await` operand (§30.5), an owning iterator's
                                 `yield return` operand — in a borrowing
                                 iterator the position carries §29.2's
                                 recorded no-marker bound) it is rejected as
                                 redundant, the diagnostic naming the
                                 announcement (§28.3). Field paths remain
                                 alternative (a): `move x.f`. Any other operand
                                 is a compile error. See §28.8.1 and §28.11. */

NewExpr         ::= "new" Type "(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "new" "(" ArgList? ")"              /* shorthand */
                              /* `new T(...) with(X := 5)` is parsed as
                                 `NewExpr` followed by a `with` PrimarySuffix;
                                 there is no separate ObjectInit production.
                                 The suffix is the record `with` of §9.5:
                                 legal when the constructed type is a record,
                                 rejected semantically when it is a class
                                . */
InitAssign      ::= Identifier ":=" Expression

LambdaExpr      ::= "async"? "lambda" "(" LambdaParams? ")"
                    (":" Type)? "=>" LambdaBody
                              /* Keyword-led (§27.3): `lambda` is
                                 reserved and begins no other expression or
                                 statement, so the reading commits at the
                                 first token (the second, after `async`) —
                                 no scan to the matching `)` is ever needed,
                                 and a parenthesized construct followed by
                                 `=>` (a when-guard arm, a grouped
                                 expression) is never a lambda prefix. The
                                 parameter parens are mandatory, including
                                 the empty pair. The optional `":" Type` is
                                 the return-type ascription (§27.3); no Type
                                 production contains `=>` (function types
                                 use `->`), so the ascription ends
                                 deterministically before the arrow. */
LambdaParams    ::= LambdaParam ("," LambdaParam)* ","?
LambdaParam     ::= FuncParamMods? Identifier (":" Type)?
                  | "_"
                  | LambdaDestructure
                              /* The bare `"_"` alternative is the parameter
                                 ignore (§27.3, §17.13): accepted, binds
                                 nothing, contributes its slot to the function
                                 type; duplicate `_` parameters are legal
                                 (nothing is named). No FuncParamMods and no
                                 annotation compose with it — a typed ignore
                                 slot is spelled by the target type (§27.4). */
LambdaDestructure ::= QualifiedName "(" LambdaSlot ("," LambdaSlot)* ","? ")"
LambdaSlot      ::= Identifier | "_" | LambdaDestructure
                              /* Positional-record destructuring in parameter
                                 position (§27.4): irrefutable
                                 binding form only — the head names the
                                 parameter's exact positional-record type; no
                                 modifiers, no annotation, no refutable
                                 pattern elements. */
LambdaBody      ::= Expression
                  | "do" Statement* "end"

IfExpr          ::= "(" "if" Expression "then" Expression
                    ("elif" Expression "then" Expression)*
                    "else" Expression ")"
                              /* The conditional atom (§20). The
                                 parentheses are part of the form: in atom-start
                                 position, "(" followed by the reserved "if"
                                 commits the reading at the second token; in
                                 call/index-argument position the atom supplies
                                 its own pair. Each condition and branch derives
                                 a full Expression (a bare throw branch is
                                 admitted anywhere); "else" is mandatory. */
CaseExpr        ::= "(" "case" Expression "of" CaseArm ("," CaseArm)* ","? ")"
                              /* The expression-position case atom: arms
                                 are Expression-bodied only (ArmBody's Statement
                                 and do-block alternatives belong to the A.6
                                 CaseStmt). "(case" commits at the second token —
                                 "case" begins no other expression. */
                              /* The former `"owned"?` scrutinee marker was
                                 deleted at v0.246 (proposal 0090). The scrutinee
                                 transfer marker (§35.5) is an ordinary scrutinee
                                 Expression whose root is an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr — `(case move x of …)`: admitted only
                                 when the scrutinee names a named owned binding
                                 of owning-choice classification; anywhere else
                                 it is a compile error. */
                              /* The scrutinee Expression is mandatory;
                                 the scrutinee-less condition-dispatch form is
                                 the separate WhenExpr below. `of` delimits the
                                 scrutinee from the first arm, so
                                 the scrutinee is a FULL Expression — no
                                 precedence restriction, no parenthesization
                                 rule — and a first pattern may begin with `-`,
                                 `..`, `..<`, or a relational token without
                                 ambiguity. */
CaseArm         ::= AltPattern ("when" Expression)? "=>" ArmBody
AltPattern      ::= Pattern ("|" Pattern)*
                              /* Pattern ALTERNATIVES are `|`-separated: the comma is exclusively the arm/slot
                                 separator, so no `=>` lookahead is needed and
                                 alternatives are available per positional slot
                                 (see PositionalPattern). `|`-joined members must
                                 be binding-free: constants, payload-free choice
                                 case names (§35.5), ranges, or
                                 relationals (§19.3). `|` never collides with
                                 bitwise-or: pattern-embedded expressions parse
                                 at Shift level or tighter (§19.3). */
WhenExpr        ::= "(" "when" WhenArm ("," WhenArm)* ","? ")"
                              /* Scrutinee-less condition dispatch (§19.1), the
                                 expression-position atom: arms are
                                 Expression-bodied only; the statement form is
                                 A.6's WhenStmt. Arms are tried in textual order;
                                 the first whose condition is `true` is selected.
                                 The construct keyword `when` is distinct from
                                 the guard `when` of a CaseArm/CatchArm —
                                 position disambiguates. */
WhenArm         ::= (Expression | "_") "=>" ArmBody
                              /* The Expression is a `bool` condition. `_` is the
                                 always-true catch-all and, if present, must be the
                                 last arm. ArmBody follows the same rules as CaseArm. */
BindExpr        ::= "(" BindClause+ Expression ")"
BindClause      ::= "var" Identifier (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                              /* The binding atom (§17.15): "(" followed
                                 by the reserved "var" — which begins no other
                                 expression — commits the reading at the second
                                 token, like the other paren atoms. Each clause
                                 introduces one single-assignment binding, in
                                 scope for the later clauses and the body; the
                                 ";" terminates the clause (no expression
                                 contains a top-level ";"). The body is one full
                                 Expression and supplies the atom's value and
                                 type. Clause initializers admit the marked
                                 transfer `move x` (a K3.4 binding transfer,
                                 §28.3); the body position does not. */
ArmBody         ::= Expression
                  | Statement                  /* valid only in a CaseStmt/WhenStmt (A.6)
                                                  or in a catch arm; reads as a single
                                                  statement whose terminating `;` ends the
                                                  arm body, the same as `do Statement end` */
                  | "do" Statement* "end"     /* type (); valid only in a CaseStmt/WhenStmt
                                                  or in a catch arm */
Pattern         ::= "_"                       /* discard */
                  | "null"                     /* null literal pattern */
                  | "var" Identifier (":" Type)?      /* binding */
                  | Constant                          /* single constant; `|`
                                                         alternatives live in
                                                         AltPattern above */
                  | RangePattern                      /* closed, half-open, or
                                                         open-ended range */
                  | RelOpPattern Shift                 /* relational; restricted
                                                         operator set, see below */
                  | Type                              /* type test */
                  | QualifiedName "(" (PositionalPatternList | NamedPatternList) ")"
                                                                /* destructuring */
                              /* The grammar does not syntactically distinguish
                                 a single-Identifier `Constant` (an enum
                                 constant or named const reference) from a
                                 single-Identifier `Type` (a type test): both
                                 productions match `Dog`. Disambiguation is
                                 by name resolution: if `Dog` resolves to a
                                 type, the pattern is a type test; otherwise
                                 it is a constant pattern. The same rule
                                 applies to QualifiedNames — `Color.Red` is a
                                 constant pattern; `System.IO.Stream` is a
                                 type-test pattern. */
PositionalPatternList ::= PositionalPattern ("," PositionalPattern)* ","?
PositionalPattern     ::= AltPattern              /* per-slot alternatives
                                                    :
                                                     TwoColor(Red | Blue, var x) */
                        | Identifier              /* naked binding,
                                                     valid only inside
                                                     positional destructuring */
NamedPatternList ::= NamedSlot ("," NamedSlot)* ","?
NamedSlot        ::= Identifier "=" AltPattern
                              /* Named-destructure slots: a destructure's
                                 slot list is positional OR named, never mixed
                                 (v1, enforced structurally). After
                                 QualifiedName "(", an Identifier followed by "="
                                 commits the named reading — "=" is not a pattern
                                 relop (RelOpPattern below) and cannot occur in
                                 pattern-embedded expressions, which parse at
                                 Shift level or tighter (§17.1). The slot
                                 Identifier is a plain member name (a qualified
                                 name before "=" does not parse). The slot RHS is
                                 a full AltPattern (per-slot alternatives,
                                 nesting); a naked identifier RHS resolves as at
                                 top level (constant or type test), never as a
                                 binding — a named-slot binding is spelled `var x`
                                 (§19.3). A constant slot is the "=" equality test
                                 (§8.4). Name resolution (records: storage
                                 fields/auto-properties; choice cases: payload
                                 field names; classes: public readable
                                 properties) and the borrow-only binding rule:
                                 §19.3; coverage: §19.6. */

RangePattern    ::= PatternBound (".." | "..<") PatternBound
                  | PatternBound ".."
                  | (".." | "..<") PatternBound
                  | ".."
PatternBound    ::= "-"? Shift
                              /* Dedicated pattern-position range form (mirrors RelOpPattern): no bare-expression
                                 leg (a lone Shift is not a range pattern) and no
                                 `step` (patterns test written bounds; stride has no
                                 membership meaning, §16.4). Bounds admit a
                                 leading `-` for negative literals. */
RelOpPattern    ::= "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">="
                              /* Pattern-form relational operators are restricted
                                 to the four ordering operators. `is`, `is not`,
                                 and `as` are not pattern relops because they
                                 belong to TypeRel and take a Type rather than
                                 a value on the right. `in` is also excluded:
                                 a membership test against a collection or range
                                 is expressed with a Range pattern (`0..10`) or
                                 a Constant pattern with alternatives, not as
                                 a relational pattern. */
                              /* The Expression on the right of a RelOpPattern
                                 must have the same type as (or be implicitly
                                 convertible to) the scrutinee's type; the type
                                 check is semantic. The grammar admits more
                                 expression forms than the rule allows — for
                                 example, `< 60..100` parses but is rejected
                                 semantically because `<` between a value and
                                 a range is not defined. */

CollectionLiteral ::= "[" (Expression ("," Expression)* ","?)? "]"
                    | "[" DictEntry ("," DictEntry)* ","? "]"                   /* dictionary */
DictEntry         ::= Expression ":" Expression

NameOfExpr      ::= "nameof" "(" QualifiedName ")"
TypeOfExpr      ::= "typeof" "(" Type ")"
DefaultExpr     ::= "default" "(" Type ")"
```

<a id="sec-constants-and-literals"></a>
### A.8 Constants and literals

```
Literal         ::= IntLiteral | FloatLiteral | CharLiteral
                  | StringLiteral | InterpString
                  | "true" | "false" | "null"
ConstExpr       ::= Expression           /* §17.14 constant expression */
Constant        ::= "-"? (IntLiteral | FloatLiteral)
                  | CharLiteral
                  | StringLiteral | "true" | "false" | "null"
                  | QualifiedName        /* enum constant, choice case (§35.5), or const reference */
```

`Literal` is the form referenced by `PrimaryAtom`; it includes interpolated strings since they are expressions. `Constant` is the restrictive form used in `case` patterns **only**; it omits `InterpString` (interpolated strings are not compile-time constants) and adds `QualifiedName` for enum constants and named constant references. `ConstExpr` is an `Expression` restricted semantically to the compile-time constant expressions of [§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions), which defines the admissible forms and the compile-time evaluation, including its faults.

---

<a id="sec-appendix-b"></a>
## Appendix B: Reserved Words

<a id="sec-reserved-keywords"></a>
### B.1 Reserved keywords

The following identifiers are keywords. Most are reserved unconditionally and may not be used as user-defined names. The **contextual keywords** (`convention`, `ensures`, `env`, `equality`, `get`, `hashable`, `invariant`, `notnull`, `of`, `old`, `operator`, `polymorphic`, `pure`, `requires`, `result`, `scoped`, `sendable`, `serialized`, `set`, `step`, `symbol`, `value`, `variadic`) have keyword meaning only in specific syntactic positions and may be used as identifiers elsewhere; see [§B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords).

**Unconditionally reserved:**

`abstract`, `and`, `as`, `async`, `await`, `base`, `bool`, `break`, `byte`, `case`, `catch`, `char`, `choice`, `class`, `closed`, `const`, `constructor`, `continue`, `decimal`, `default`, `destructor`, `do`, `double`, `elif`, `else`, `end`, `enum`, `extension`, `extern`, `false`, `finally`, `float`, `for`, `if`, `import`, `in`, `int`, `interface`, `internal`, `is`, `lambda`, `long`, `method`, `mod`, `module`, `move`, `nameof`, `new`, `not`, `null`, `or`, `out`, `owned`, `override`, `private`, `property`, `protected`, `public`, `readonly`, `record`, `ref`, `return`, `sbyte`, `sealed`, `short`, `static`, `string`, `then`, `this`, `throw`, `true`, `try`, `type`, `typeof`, `uint`, `ulong`, `ushort`, `using`, `var`, `virtual`, `when`, `where`, `while`, `with`, `yield`.

**Contextual (see [§B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords)):**

`convention`, `ensures`, `env`, `equality`, `get`, `hashable`, `invariant`, `notnull`, `of`, `old`, `operator`, `polymorphic`, `pure`, `requires`, `result`, `scoped`, `sendable`, `serialized`, `set`, `step`, `symbol`, `value`, `variadic`.

All keywords are lowercase. Type identifiers in PascalCase (`Object`, `Array`, `Type`, `Exception`, `IDisposable`, `Task`, etc.) are not keywords; they are names defined by the standard library or by compiler intrinsics.

**The reserved token `_`.** The bare underscore is reserved as a **token**, not as a keyword in the word sense: it is held out of the identifier namespace like a punctuation symbol — the discard/wildcard of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_) — and can never be declared or read as a name ([§1.3](#sec-identifiers)). Identifiers merely containing underscores are unaffected. (Holding a token out of the identifier namespace so a form stays re-introducible or unambiguous is [§B.3](#sec-future-reservations)'s existing discipline; `_` is that discipline applied permanently.)

<a id="sec-contextual-keywords"></a>
### B.2 Contextual keywords

The following keywords from [§B.1](#sec-reserved-keywords) carry meaning only in specific syntactic positions and may also appear as identifiers in other positions. The compiler distinguishes by context.

| Keyword | Reserved context | May be used as identifier |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | The `where T: value` constraint; the implicit setter parameter | Anywhere else: as a property name, a parameter name, etc. |
| `notnull` | The `where T: notnull` constraint | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `step` | After a range expression | Anywhere else |
| `convention` | After the library name in an `extern` block header | Anywhere else |
| `get`, `set` | Property and indexer accessor declarations (block form) and auto-property accessor visibility shorthand | Anywhere else |
| `operator` | After `static method` in an operator overload declaration | Anywhere else |
| `serialized` | The `serialized` clause on a positional field, auto-property, or enum constant (field-name customization, [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)). Within that clause, `skip` and `optional` are likewise contextual and are not reserved | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `equality` | The `equality skip` clause on a positional field, auto-property, explicit record field, or choice payload field (per-member auto-equality exclusion, [§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)). Within that clause, `skip` is likewise contextual and is not reserved — exactly `serialized`'s row | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `polymorphic` | The class-body `polymorphic (…)` registry member (class serialization synthesis, [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `of` | The scrutinee/arm delimiter in a `case` expression ([§19](#sec-the-case-construct)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `scoped` | The storage-bounded modifier on a function-typed parameter or field, on a class/interface-typed borrow parameter, and its call-site argument marker ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters), [§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `symbol` | The `:= symbol "…"` alias clause of an extern declaration ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `variadic` | The `variadic(N)` clause after an extern symbol alias ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `sendable` | The `where T: sendable` constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `hashable` | The `where T: hashable` constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `pure` | The member-modifier slot ([§11.5](#sec-modifier-order), [§22.15](#sec-pure-members)) and the `pure get` accessor form | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `requires`, `ensures` | Opening a contract clause in the clause region of a method or constructor declaration ([§22.16](#sec-contract-clauses)); the keyword reading always wins there | Anywhere else: as identifiers |
| `invariant` | Member-leading position in a class body, optionally after `static` ([§22.16](#sec-class-invariants)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `old` | Inside `ensures` clauses, where followed by `(` ([§22.16](#sec-clause-evaluation)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `result` | Throughout `ensures` clauses — the keyword reading always wins there; a parameter named `result` is not denotable in an `ensures` clause (rename it; `out`-parameter renames are call-site-invisible, [§22.5](#sec-optional-parameters-and-named-arguments)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `env` | The user-data slot marker in an extern parameter list and the corresponding position in an extern callback's function type ([§32.8](#sec-callbacks)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier — including as an extern parameter **name** (`env: IntPtr`; the following `:` disambiguates, grammar A.3). Inside an extern callback's **function type** the marker reading always wins: a user type named `env` is not denotable in that one position (rename or alias the type) |

The setter parameter is named `value` by convention; it is not a true keyword in that role and may be shadowed inside the setter body (though doing so is poor style).

`when`, `where`, `with`, and `yield` are reserved everywhere — although they appear only in specific syntactic positions in practice, the grammar treats them as full keywords for clarity.

<a id="sec-not-vs-notnull"></a>
#### `not` vs `notnull`

`not` (boolean negation, [§6.5](#sec-bitwise-operations)) is unconditionally reserved; it cannot appear as an identifier in any position. `notnull` (the generic constraint, [§14.2](#sec-constraints)) is contextual; it is reserved only in the `where T: notnull` position and may otherwise be used as an identifier (a parameter name, a field name, etc.). The two are distinct tokens — there is no relationship between their lexical statuses despite the visual similarity.

The two-token sequence `is not` ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators), type test combined with negation) is recognized by the parser specifically in the relational position; it does not require `not` to be contextual. `is not` parses as a single relational operator wherever a relational operator is expected, and `not` outside that two-token sequence remains the unary boolean operator. So `x is not Foo` and `not (x is Foo)` are both legal expressions with the same truth value but different narrowing behavior ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators)).

<a id="sec-future-reservations"></a>
### B.3 Future reservations

This version of the language reserves exactly one identifier for future use: **`event`**. It was the keyword of the retired event member kind ([§24](#sec-events)); it is held out of the identifier namespace so that pre-retirement declarations fail with a reserved-word diagnostic rather than parsing `event` as an identifier, and so that a one-line declaration form remains re-introducible without a breaking change. Any other new keywords in future revisions will be drawn from new compound forms or from words not currently used as identifiers in the standard library.

---

<a id="sec-appendix-c"></a>
## Appendix C: Compiler-Enforced Invariants

This appendix consolidates the invariants the compiler enforces. It is a checklist for implementers and a reference for programmers wanting to know which classes of error are caught at compile time.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-type-system"></a>
### C.1 Type system

- Every variable, field, parameter, and return value has a declared or inferred type.
- The bare token `_` is never a declarable or readable name ([§1.3](#sec-identifiers), [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)): a declaration naming `_` — a local (`var _`, `const _`), a method or constructor parameter, a field, property, method, type, module, enum constant, choice case, loop label, or alias — is a compile error, as are `out var _`, `ref _` in argument position, a pattern binding (`case x of var _ =>`), a catch-arm binding (`catch var _: E =>`), a binding-atom clause (`(var _ := E; body)`, [§17.15](#sec-the-binding-atom)), and any expression-position read of `_`; each draws the remedy-naming diagnostic of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)'s rejected-positions list. The sanctioned `_` forms are the discard/wildcard positions of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_), the anonymous owning binding `using var _`/`await using var _` ([§28.10](#sec-using-var) — the ordinary `using var` type ascription retained), and the lambda-parameter and `for var _` ignores ([§27.3](#sec-lambda-expressions), [§21.4](#sec-the-for-statement)); a type ascription or parameter modifier on a bare **ignore** is likewise rejected (an ignore's type comes from context, never an annotation).
- Implicit conversions occur only as listed in [§5.1](#sec-implicit-conversions).
- When more than one overload is applicable to a call only because arguments match through different implicit conversions ([§5.1](#sec-implicit-conversions)), the call resolves to the candidate that is unambiguously better — exact on every argument where another candidate converts, and never worse. An exact match is preferred over any implicit conversion; built-in implicit conversions are not ranked against one another. If no candidate is unambiguously better, the call is ambiguous and is a compile error citing the candidates ([§22.6](#sec-implicit-conversion-ranking)); the programmer disambiguates with an explicit cast. This mirrors overloaded method-reference resolution ([§27.6](#sec-method-references-to-overloaded-methods)). A candidate applicable without filling any parameter default is preferred over one that fills defaults ([§22.6](#sec-implicit-conversion-ranking)).
- Generic-method type arguments are inferred per [§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference): explicit lists are all-or-nothing; bindings for a type parameter must agree exactly (no common-supertype join); lambdas bind in a second phase; the call's target type only completes parameters the arguments left unbound; a failed inference makes that candidate inapplicable; and an otherwise-tied non-generic candidate beats a generic one — the last comparison before ambiguity, after the defaulted-arity tie-break ([§22.6](#sec-overloading)). Class/record-level type arguments are never inferred from constructor arguments.
- A choice declares at least one case; case names are distinct and do not collide with member names; a choice has no destructors, constructors, instance fields, storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types; a choice type does not contain itself through value-typed components ([§35.1](#sec-choice-declaration)).
- `default(C)` is a compile error for every choice type C; choices never satisfy `where T: new()` ([§35.10](#sec-choice-default-with), [§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- A non-nullable reference may not be assigned `null`.
- A nullable value may not be dereferenced without a null check or `!`.
- Every non-nullable field is assigned in every constructor or has a field initializer.
- Every non-nullable local is assigned before its first read.
- Definite-assignment analysis applies uniformly to instance and static non-nullable reference fields. A static constructor body's `try`/`catch` is subject to the same flow analysis as any constructor body: every path through the static initializer (including catch-and-recover paths) must definitely-assign every non-nullable reference static field.
- A type's `Equals` override requires a matching `GetHashCode` override.
- A class with one or more `abstract` members must itself be `abstract` (or `closed`, [§11.7](#sec-static-classes)).
- An abstract or `closed` class cannot be instantiated with `new`.
- Member hiding is forbidden: a derived class cannot reuse the name of an inherited member **visible at its declaration site** unless overriding a virtual member ([§12.2](#sec-hiding-is-not-allowed) — an invisible base member (`private`, or cross-module `internal`) does not block the name; the two are then distinct members with no override or overload relationship).
- An override must match the base member's visibility, return type, parameter types, **and parameter modifiers (`ref`, `out`, `owned`, `scoped`)** exactly, except that a parameter may widen `T` to `T?` ([§12.1](#sec-members-are-non-virtual-by-default) — the same contravariant allowance as interface implementations); the widening is monotone down the override chain.
- An inheritance cycle is rejected: no type may, directly or transitively, list itself among its base classes or extended interfaces ([§12.10](#sec-inheritance-cycles)).
- A type may not declare two members that are indistinguishable: two fields, properties, or nested types of the same name, or two methods, constructors, or operator overloads of the same name that are not distinguishable as overloads ([§22.6](#sec-overloading)), are a compile error; likewise a non-overloadable member (field, property, nested type) may not share its name with any other member regardless of kind. Legal overloads are unaffected ([§11.3](#sec-member-body)).
- A **method-local** `record`/`enum` declaration ([§21.10](#sec-local-type-declarations)) is an ordinary nominal record/enum by every §9/§10 rule, registered in a body-scoped type space: it carries no visibility keyword and no generic parameters (v1), is scoped to its enclosing block like a local variable, must precede first use, may not appear in any member signature, may not reference an enclosing generic parameter, and may not shadow a type name visible at its declaration or clash with another declaration in the same body's declaration space. A local `choice`, `class`, or `interface` is rejected.
- Neither `owned` (on an ordinary or `out` parameter) nor `scoped` distinguishes overloads: two members differing only in these modifiers clash ([§22.6](#sec-overloading) — the `out`/`out owned` carve-out is withdrawn).
- Variant generic parameters (`in`, `out`) appear only in the appropriate position.
- A variant assignment whose source has a value-type type argument is rejected; the type itself (e.g. `IEnumerable<int>`) is fully usable, only the variant conversion is forbidden ([§12.9](#sec-variance)).
- Boxing a borrow-bearing record or a borrow-carrying inline array is subject to the same borrow-lifetime constraints as the unboxed value; the boxed value may not escape the source scope ([§8.6](#sec-boxing)). Move-only inline arrays (owning forms) cannot be boxed.
- `default(T)` is rejected for non-nullable reference types, for records whose declared fields include non-nullable references, and for inline arrays whose element type is a non-nullable reference type (including `[N owned]T` non-nullable owning forms).
- `default(T)` on an enum type with no declared zero-value constant is a compile error, as are `new T()` at such a substitution and default initialization of enum-typed storage ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)).
- An integer-to-enum cast `E(n)` is checked against the declared constants ([§5.4](#sec-enum-casts)): a constant operand equal to no declared constant is a compile error at the cast site; a non-constant operand equal to no declared constant raises `OverflowException` at runtime. No value of an enum type exists that is not equal to a declared constant.
- A shift count outside `0..width−1` of the left operand's type ([§6.5](#sec-bitwise-operations)) is a compile error when the count is a constant — including in constant-expression evaluation ([§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions)) — and raises `OverflowException` at runtime otherwise; `<<=`/`>>=` inherit the rule ([§6.6](#sec-compound-assignments)).
- A collection literal targeting a reference type (`Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>`, `Set<T>`, `Dictionary<K, V>`, etc., or a user-defined type via the `FromCollectionLiteral` factory of [§15.4.1](#sec-the-user-defined-sequence-literal-protocol)) produces an owned value; the result must reach an owned location ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)). For the user-defined case the owned value is the factory's `owned C<T>` return. A collection literal targeting an inline-array type (`[N]T`) produces a value, with the usual value-type rules; ownership obligations apply only when the array has `[N owned]…` slots ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)).
- Nullable field or property access — other than the narrowing `readonly`-field form — without copying to a local is rejected; local variables and `readonly` fields (one field off an admitted root, v0.214) are narrowed ([§7.4](#sec-member-access-on-nullable-values)).
- An `end`-label that is supplied — an identifier for named constructs, or a construct keyword (with operator token where applicable) for keyword-labelled constructs — must match the construct it closes; a mismatch is a compile error. The unlabelled form `end;` is always valid ([§1.6](#sec-statements-and-termination)).
- A `closed` class may be subclassed only within its declaring module; external subclasses are rejected. The spelling `sealed abstract` is rejected, the diagnostic naming `closed` ([§11.7](#sec-static-classes)).
- An enum implementing an interface must provide matching public members for every interface member.
- Calling `.Equals(Object?)`, `.Equals(T)`, or `.GetHashCode()` directly on a non-auto-hashable body record ([§9.2](#sec-body-records)) is a compile error at the call site; the user must declare custom equality, mark the disqualifying member `equality skip` ([§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)), or simplify the record to an auto-hashable form. Calls through an `Object`-typed receiver bypass the static-type check and reach the inherited `Object.Equals`/`GetHashCode` at runtime (reference equality / identity-based hash), but this is rare in practice.
- A storage component marked `equality skip` ([§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)) is removed from the auto-equality membership computation — excluded from the generated `=`/`<>`, `Equals`, and `GetHashCode`, exempt from the admissible-component requirement, and unable to disqualify its record or choice — while every other role (storage, `with`, `ToString`, serialization participation) is untouched; the generated `=` and `GetHashCode` compute over the same reduced set, so equal values hash equal by construction. The clause on a computed property, method, static member, enum constant, choice case, or class field is a compile error (the [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis) inert-annotation discipline); on a member of a record whose `Equals`/`GetHashCode` override suppresses the package it is meaningful, not an error.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-visibility"></a>
### C.2 Visibility

- Every class member declares its visibility explicitly, except `static constructor`, `destructor`, and the `polymorphic` registry (which carry no visibility keyword).
- Every type appearing in a member's signature — field type, parameter type, return type, property type, indexer parameter and result type, types named in `where` constraints — is at least as visible as the member. The rule applies at every visibility level except `private`, which is unconstrained.
- A class's base class and implemented interfaces are at least as visible as the class.
- Top-level types are `public` or `internal` only.
- An explicit accessor visibility is no less restrictive than the property's overall visibility.
- An override declares the same visibility as the base member.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-resource-management"></a>
### C.3 Resource management

- An owning-classified choice ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) is a move-only value type: disposal disposes the active case's `owned` payloads exactly once, on every path — scope end, exception edges, drop-on-overwrite (which, for choices, disposes the displaced value automatically), discard, or a consuming match ([§35.5](#sec-owning-match)) ([K3](#sec-kernel-k3), [K5](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- An owning-classified choice cannot be boxed, is not directly sendable, and does not implement `IDisposable`; its disposal is discharged by its holder ([§35.8](#sec-choice-boxing), [§35.12](#sec-choice-sendability)).

- `Dispose()` is generated for every non-static class ([K4.1](#sec-kernel-k4)'s backstop machinery).
- The compiler-generated `Dispose()` is thread-safe with respect to idempotency: concurrent calls execute disposal exactly once ([§28.2](#sec-the-idisposable-contract); K4.1).
- Owned fields are restricted to class- or interface-typed fields ([§28.5](#sec-owned-fields); not `string`, not function types, not value types; [K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1) + [K1.7](#sec-kernel-k1)).
- Assignment to an owned field or plain-`var` owned local disposes the displaced live value before storing (drop-on-overwrite, [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields), [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3); null/moved-from displaced values dispose nothing; RHS evaluated first).
- Owned values may not escape: *transferring* an owned field out (a `move`, or a fresh owning value) requires an `owned` return type; a bare owned-field read may be returned through a non-`owned` return as a borrow of the receiver ([§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)) — `Task`-family returns excepted (the `Task`-family production bullet below); assigning a freshly-produced or `move`d owned value to a non-owned field is rejected ([K9.1](#sec-kernel-k9) + K1.7 + [K2.3](#sec-kernel-k2); an owned field's *bare read* reaches such a field only as a borrow, governed by §28.3's borrowed-field store rule — §28.6).
- A `new` expression's result, and any owned local, is disposed exactly once on every path ([K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3) + [K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3)): it either reaches an owned location / explicit `Dispose()` / `move` / return, or is **auto-dropped at scope end** ([§28.3](#sec-owned-local-discharge-requirement)). An implicit auto-drop of a plain-`var` owned local raises a **must-use warning** (not an error); the warning is suppressed by `using var`, explicit disposal, discard, move, or return. Discard `_ := …` of an owned class or move-only value is permitted (disposes at end of statement; [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3)). For trivial-dispose classes, no discharge is demanded of the program: the compiler frees the undischarged value at its owner's release point — no warning, no user code (K1.6; [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)). Implicit boxing is not subject to this rule ([§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer)).
- A `static` method or operator whose declared return type (nullability stripped) is a class or interface type must announce its classification in the signature — `owned`, a `Task`-family type, a §29.3/§30.7 iterable or enumerator interface, or a bare type parameter with a non-empty potential source set; any other such static signature (including an empty-set bare-type-parameter return, spellable as `owned T` under §28.1's per-instantiation erasure) is a compile error at the declaration ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)). For a **bare-type-parameter** return — including one inherited by an implementation or override of a generic declaration — the sources are identifiable from the signature: at class/interface instantiations the call is a **borrow** of the receiver and the T-reaching plain arguments (union of source-liveness), with an empty potential source set the signature is rejected at the declaration; callee-side, such a return admits plain-parameter- and receiver-sourced borrows, and under an empty set it must supply fresh or owned values — the static-storage admission (property-getter-only) does not extend to it ([§28.3](#sec-bare-type-parameter-returns)). A concrete-typed static **method** likewise may not return a static-storage borrow: a bare `static` field read (any admissible form — `owned`, §22.13-exempt `readonly`, or a §22.12-rule-2 admitted mutable static) passes through a non-`owned` return only from a static property getter — a cached instance is re-exposed through a static property (the `T.P` producers row) or transferred with an `owned` return ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)). (Derives: the declaration-site static-return rule ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)); the sourced cases derive: [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2) — static storage is [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source.)
- An owning-collection or owning-wrapper return type (`OwningArray<T>`, `Shared<T>`, etc. — **not** the `Task` family) declared without `owned` produces a **borrow** (the `Owning*` name denotes element ownership, orthogonal to the `owned` container qualifier); the general borrow-return rules apply — a bare owning-collection *field* read is returnable (source: receiver), a borrowed local/parameter with no outliving source is not, and a `move`d field or fresh owning value requires an `owned` return ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)). ([K1.5](#sec-kernel-k1) + K2.4; the `Task`-family-only mint keying is axiom [A2](#sec-axiom-register).)
