- A **call** whose declared (pre-substitution, nullability-stripped) return type is a `Task`-family type (`Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`) produces an **owned** task at the call site — instance, static, extension, interface, or function-value invocation; no factory warning ([§28.3](#sec-producers); [K6.3](#sec-kernel-k6) — the family keying is axiom A2). Callee-side, the unmarked `Task`-family return type is container-ownership-transferring: a non-`async` body returns a fresh or owned task on every path, and returning a stored task borrow (a bare field or property read, a plain parameter, a captured binding) is rejected — stored tasks are re-exposed through properties, fields, or collection slots, whose reads are borrows ([§30.11](#sec-taskcompletionsourcet-and-ownedtaskcompletionsourcet), [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)(b)).
- Explicit `Dispose()` requires an **owned receiver** (owned local/parameter, `using var`, owned temporary, `move` result, or an owned field/slot read by its declaring type's code) ([K3.10](#sec-kernel-k3)); `Dispose()` through a borrow is a compile error, with **no exception** (element borrows from borrowing-family collections included; the A8 tombstone records the retired carve). For a *borrowed owning collection* every other operation, including the mutating / transferring ones (`Add`/`Insert`/`Remove*`/`Clear`/`Drain`/`Pop*`/indexer-set), is memory-safe on a borrow and remains available (Bezel's borrowed collections are mutable — the pass-and-fill idiom) ([§28.6](#sec-borrowed-owning-collections); [K1](#sec-kernel-k1)'s container-vs-element obligation split).
- An unbound owned temporary — the result of an `owned`-returning producer that is not bound, `move`d, returned, or transferred, used only by borrowing operations within its expression — is disposed exactly once: at the end of that full expression after its uses complete, or during unwinding (reverse order of production) when the expression is exited by an exception before the temporary is consumed ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries); K1 + K3.15 + [K8.1](#sec-kernel-k8)).
- A binding-atom binding whose initializer is an owned production ([§17.15](#sec-the-binding-atom)) is a named unbound owned temporary bounded by the atom: disposed exactly once — at the atom's completion (after the body, reverse clause order) if undischarged, during unwinding on the exception edge, or not at all by the boundary pass when a [K3](#sec-kernel-k3) consuming position inside the atom discharged it; a borrow or frame sourced by an atom binding may not escape the atom ([K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8)/[K8.5](#sec-kernel-k8)).
- An `out owned` parameter is a callee-local owned slot until normal return (copy-out, [§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)): a value assigned to it is disposed by the callee's exception-path discharge if the callee subsequently throws, and transfers to the caller's recipient exactly on normal return — the assignment obligation binds on return paths only, and the caller-side `out using var` obligation attaches only on normal-completion paths ([§22.4](#sec-inline-out-declarations)). ([K3](#sec-kernel-k3) with the callee-local slot as its scope; edge parity: K3.15.)
- `using var` variables may not be reassigned (axiom [A5](#sec-axiom-register)).
- Records may not have `owned` fields, may not have inline-array fields with the `owned` slot marker, may not have destructors, may not implement `IDisposable` (K1.7 — copy-semantics holders cannot hold obligations).
- At a control-flow merge point, a variable that was owned on one branch and borrowed on the other is rejected ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows); [K7.3](#sec-kernel-k7)). The two branches must be equalized before the merge.
- A method reference that captures a borrowed receiver is subject to the same closure-escape rules as a lambda capturing a borrow ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types); K2.3).
- A borrow-bearing record or a borrow-carrying inline array may be stored in a static field only when every reference-typed field (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value is null (the null-source form, [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal); K2.3 — the always-live holder admits only borrow-free values).
- A trivial-dispose class (no destructor, no `owned` fields of non-trivial-dispose type, no fields of owning-inline-array type, no non-trivial base) has its discharge performed by the compiler: undischarged `new` expressions are not warned about, `_ := newTrivialClass();` is permitted, and every undischarged trivial-dispose value is freed — logical disposal (flag) plus reclamation, no user code — at its statically-known owner's release point ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types), [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal); K1.6 — empty user-visible obligation content).
- A `_ := expression;` discard statement ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)) is permitted for any owned class, interface, or move-only value — it disposes the value at end of statement (calling `Dispose()` on the runtime type, so it is correct for any interface implementation; K3.9 + [K4.2](#sec-kernel-k4)). It is rejected only for `Task` and `Task<T>` (disposing a task abandons a running operation; use `Task.FireAndForget` — a semantic, not a leak, restriction; axiom [A6](#sec-axiom-register)).
- A class implementing `IAsyncDisposable` without a destructor receives a compiler warning ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal)).
- The `move x.f` expression ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression); K9.1) is permitted only when `f` is an owned instance field; the field is left in moved-from state. Within the surrounding method, every control-flow path from the move site to the method's exit (normal return, throw, fall-through, `yield break`) must execute an assignment `x.f := value;` between the move and the exit — including paths exited by exceptions raised by intervening throwable expressions. Failure to satisfy the rule is a compile error ([K9.2](#sec-kernel-k9)).
- The `move coll[i]` expression ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression), [§28.11](#sec-collections-do-not-own-elements)) is permitted only when `coll` is an owned-element collection; the slot is left in moved-from state (K9.1). The same field-restoration rule applies (K9.2, per-slot), with constant indices tracked per-slot and non-constant indices tracked conservatively at the whole-collection level.
- Owned-element collections (`OwningArray<T>`, `OwningDictionary<K, V>`, etc.) own their elements: the owned-ingress members accept owned arguments (`Add`/`Insert` on the `IOwningCollection<T>` conformers; `Push`/`Enqueue` on `OwningStack<T>`/`OwningQueue<T>`), the indexer-set disposes the previous value, `Remove`/`RemoveAt`/`Clear` dispose elements on the types that declare them, and `Dispose` cascades to every element. The `Drain` method transfers ownership of elements out of the collection in iteration order. Default iteration produces borrows; ownership is transferred only via `Drain` or the dedicated `Pop*` methods ([§28.11](#sec-collections-do-not-own-elements)). (K1 per slot; the two-family design is axiom [A9](#sec-axiom-register).)
- Iterator yield ownership is determined by the iterator method's declared return type ([§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for) "Iterator yield ownership"; [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6) — announcement by declared type). For an iterator returning `IEnumerable<T>` or `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` that yields owned class-typed values (fresh producers and `move` results — an unmarked named-binding yield is a re-borrow, not a transfer, [§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for)), the enumerator owns each yielded value and the consumer's iteration variable is a borrow. For an iterator returning `IOwningEnumerable<T>`, `IOwningEnumerator<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerable<T>`, or `IOwningAsyncEnumerator<T>`, ownership transfers from enumerator to consumer at each `MoveNext` (or `MoveNextAsync`); the consumer's iteration variable is owned; it is discharged by the program or auto-dropped at the body's end with the must-use warning (§28.3).
- In an owning iterator, `yield return x;` on a named owned binding is an announced consume (the declared owning return type is the announcement; the yield takes no marker, a redundant `yield return move x;` being rejected at the announced target, [§28.3](#sec-move-semantics-for-owned-locals)) and **joins the consume-site freeze** ([K5.1](#sec-kernel-k5)); in a borrowing iterator the same unmarked read is a re-borrow of the frame-resident binding ([§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for), [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)).
- A discard statement `_ := x;` over a named owned binding is an announced consume: disposed at end of the discard statement, the binding left explicitly-disposed; the form takes no transfer marker (`_ := move x;` is not a form — the sink is the announcement), and the consume-site freeze does not apply ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_), [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows); K4.2 + [K5.3](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- A closure may read a captured owned binding (as a borrow) but may not assign to it, transfer from it, or dispose it ([§28.3](#sec-captured-owned-bindings); K2 + [K5.5](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- The must-use warning covers undischarged `owned` parameters of iterators and async methods, attached at the parameter declaration ([§28.3](#sec-owned-local-discharge-requirement), [§29.8](#sec-iterators-with-owned-parameters), [§30.1](#sec-async-methods); K3.14).
- A returned deferred-activation frame may carry only parameter- or receiver-sourced borrows — its carried sources including its plain function-typed arguments' capture-set contributions ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)); carrying a scope-bound local's, `using var`'s, or temporary's borrow out through the return, directly or through a callback's capture, is rejected ([§28.3](#sec-returning-a-deferred-activation-frame); K6.2 + K2.4).
- A fresh-producer element of non-trivial-dispose class type in a borrowing-family collection literal is rejected (bind the source first, or use the owning family); a fresh element of trivial-dispose type is not a borrow but a **fresh node of the literal tree**, aggregate-owned under the literal-tree ownership rule and freed with its aggregate at the aggregate owner's release point; `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set stay under the existing admissions, with a **fresh unbound owned temporary of class type** — trivial-dispose, `Task`-family, and other non-trivial-dispose alike — drawing the §15.4 store warning (v0.243) ([§15.4](#sec-collection-literals), [§28.11](#sec-borrowing-collections); [K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8) + K2.3 — the temporary dies at the statement's end).
- A stdlib §5 class-element terminal accessor or no-selector aggregation call — `Aggregate(seed, fold)` on its receiver leg only — whose receiver's statically-traced provenance roots at a **directly-called same-compilation-unit iterator with an enumerator-owned fresh yield**, or a lazy chain over one, draws the §29.11 terminal-accessor provenance warning (v0.243): the element borrow is dead on arrival (certain under all-fresh yields, possible under mixed); the silent-root set is normative at §29.11, and acceptance is unchanged ([§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration), stdlib [§5](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-collections-linq); [§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership)'s yield classification).
- Implicit discharge — auto-drop, exception-path cleanup, drop-on-overwrite, cascades, frame teardown — always takes the synchronous `Dispose()` path; only `await using` (or an awaited direct `DisposeAsync()`) runs asynchronous cleanup ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal); the implicit forms are K3.14/K3.15, K3.11, [K9](#sec-kernel-k9)'s cascade, and [K6](#sec-kernel-k6)'s frame teardown).

<a id="sec-appendix-c-generics"></a>
### C.4 Generics

- `where T: sendable` substitutions are types whose sendable derived type property ([§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)) holds; checked per instantiation after substitution ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).

- `where T: notnull` substitutions are non-nullable types; a nullable type, value or reference, does not satisfy the constraint.
- `where T: class` substitutions are non-nullable reference types: classes (including `Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>`), interfaces, `string`, function types.
- `where T: value` substitutions are non-nullable value types: records, enums, primitives, inline arrays (all forms, including owning `[N owned]…` forms — see [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types) for restrictions on copy operations in the generic body), the unit type. A nullable value type (e.g. `int?`) does not satisfy the constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- `where T: SomeClass` substitutions are non-nullable subtypes of `SomeClass` — class types only (no interfaces, since interfaces do not extend classes).
- `where T: IFoo` substitutions are non-nullable types conforming to `IFoo` per the [§14.2](#sec-constraints) conformance rule: classes implementing it (directly, by inheritance, or implicitly — `IDisposable`), records and enums implementing it directly, interfaces extending it (directly or transitively), primitives conforming through their stdlib declarations or the compiler-provided conformances ([§14.2](#sec-constraints) clause 5, [§11.8](#sec-static-interface-members)), and type parameters whose constraints guarantee it.
- `where T: new()` substitutions are class types with a `public` parameterless constructor, or value types whose `default(T)` is well-defined; `new T()` for a value substitution is `default(T)` ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- Constraint combinations are checked for consistency (`class, value` is rejected).
- Inside an unconstrained generic body, `T` is treated conservatively as possibly nullable.
- `?` is idempotent under substitution: `T?` with T = `U?` denotes `U?` (no two-level optional; [§7.10](#sec-generics-and-nullability)).
- Type-bound constraints (`where T: class`, `where T: SomeClass`, `where T: IFoo`) and `where T: notnull` make T non-nullable inside the body.
- `owned` is not admitted on generic type arguments ([§14.4](#sec-owned-as-a-generic-argument)). The owning collection and task types are separate named classes (`OwningArray<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, etc., declared in stdlib [§4](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-collections-generic) and [§6](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-threading)); each carries `where T: class` (or `where V: class` for `OwningDictionary<K, V>`) as part of its declaration.
- Type-argument inference for generic methods follows [§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference); constraints are checked after inference, on the completed substitution, and are not inference sources.

<a id="sec-methods-constructors-and-accessors"></a>
### C.5 Methods, constructors, and accessors

- Modifier order matches [§11.5](#sec-modifier-order).
- A constructor's `base(...)` or `this(...)` call appears in the chain position before the body, not as a statement in the body (see [§12.8](#sec-constructor-chaining) and grammar A.4 `CtorChain`).
- Field initializers run exactly once per instance construction — as step 2 of the constructor whose chain position holds `base(...)` or the implicit `base()`; a `this(...)`-chaining constructor skips them ([§22.8](#sec-field-initializers)).
- A class with a primary constructor permits `base(...)` only on the primary constructor; non-primary constructors must chain with `this(...)`.
- A static constructor takes no parameters and no access modifier.
- A method declared `async` returns `Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerator<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerable<T>`, or `IOwningAsyncEnumerator<T>`.
- A method using `yield return`/`yield break` does not also use plain `return`.
- An `async` method, `async` lambda, or iterator method (sync or async) declares no `ref` or `out` parameter; an `async` lambda's target function type carries no `ref`/`out` slot ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods), [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods)).
- `yield` does not appear in lambdas, in `try` blocks whose surrounding statement has a `catch`, or in catch arm bodies or `finally` blocks.
- `return` does not appear in `finally` blocks.
- `break` and `continue` appear only inside loops of the same callable body; a labeled form names the loop label of a lexically enclosing loop statement of that body; neither exits a `finally` block (the target loop — labeled or unlabeled — must not enclose the `finally`; [§21.5](#sec-break-and-continue), [§31.2](#sec-try-catch-finally)).
- A loop label appears only on `while`/`for`/`await for` statements, duplicates no loop label in scope at its declaration, and — when the loop's `end` carries a closer label — matches it per [§1.6](#sec-statements-and-termination): the loop label if the loop has one, the introducing keyword otherwise.
- `++` and `--` appear only as statements.
- A compound assignment evaluates its target once — each LHS constituent once, getter and setter each once ([§6.6](#sec-compound-assignments), [§17.6](#sec-increment-decrement-on-indexer-slots)); its result stores back directly, or through the checked narrow-integer write-back where [§6.6](#sec-compound-assignments) admits it — any other type mismatch is a compile error.
- Bare `throw` (the expression form without an operand, and equivalently the statement form `throw;`) appears only inside a catch arm body.
- The operand of `throw expr` is an owned expression whose static type is `Exception` or a class deriving from it; primitive, `string`, record, enum, inline-array, unit, function-typed, `Object`-typed, and interface-typed operands are rejected, as are borrowed class references ([§31.1](#sec-throwing)).
- A field initializer does not reference `this`, instance members, or virtual methods.
- A synchronous observation of `this` in a constructor body (instance call, argument, store, type test) occurs only after every [§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)-strict field of the declaring class is definitely assigned; in the `base(...)`/`this(...)` argument position it is always rejected ([§22.7](#sec-observing-this-during-construction)).
- A `virtual`/`override`/`abstract` member is not called on `this` from a constructor body unless the class is `sealed` and not `abstract`; `base.M()` is exempt ([§22.7](#sec-observing-this-during-construction)).
- Reference-typed fields are null-initialized before construction begins; a checked-mode read of a non-nullable reference field still at the watermark raises `NullReferenceException` ([§22.7](#sec-observing-this-during-construction)).
- A `bool`-returning method's `when true`/`when false` nullability postcondition is admitted only on an `out`/`out owned` parameter of nullable type; every path of the declaring body that returns the stated constant must leave the parameter provably non-null, and an override must repeat the clause exactly ([§22.4](#sec-out-nullability-postcondition)).

<a id="sec-async"></a>
### C.6 Async

- `async` does not combine with `abstract` on a method.
- `await` appears only inside `async` methods, `async` lambdas, and the synchronous prefix of `await for`.
- `await` does not appear in static field initializers or static constructor bodies.
- `await using` appears only inside async contexts.
- The `with` clause in `await for ... with token` must be of type `CancellationToken`.
- Awaiting a `Task<T>` for class T (Pattern A — axiom [A3](#sec-axiom-register)'s shared-borrow container) requires the awaited task expression to be an **admitted borrow source** per [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal) (each admitted position an instance of K2's source kinds): a named location — an owning one, or a plain borrowed local or parameter of `Task<T>` — or an unbound owned temporary whose borrowed result is confined to the full expression. The named locations **include**: a reference to a `using var`/`await using var`-bound local of `Task<T>`, a plain owned local, a plain (non-`owned`) local or parameter of `Task<T>` (the binding's scope bounds the borrow, its borrow chain carrying the caller-side residual), an `owned` parameter, an `owned` field of `this` or of any other live root (a task-typed field path rooted at a live object — §30.5), an admitted static `Task<T>` field, an indexer access on an owning collection of `Task<T>`, or an iteration variable from a borrowing iteration over an array of tasks. A producer call whose result is directly consumed by a Pattern A return in the enclosing async method is also admitted, as is an **unbound owned temporary** task whose borrowed result is confined to the same full expression (`Process(await Producer())`) — disposed at the expression's end per [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries). A bare `var x := await Producer();` whose `Producer()` returns `Task<T>` for class T remains rejected — the borrow would outlive the temporary that sources it.
- `await` on a `OwningTask<T>` (Pattern B — A3's owned-transfer container) must appear in an owned-consuming context ([K3](#sec-kernel-k3)'s positions) — a `using var` (or `await using var`) right-hand side, an `owned` parameter argument, an `owned` return expression, or any other position the type system requires the resulting value to be discharged. The first await spends an `OwningTask<T>` regardless of outcome. When the operand is **owned**, the await consumes it on all edges — an announced kill ([K3.5](#sec-kernel-k3) + K4.2): no call-site marker, no consume-site freeze, disposed-flag backstop ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal), [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)) — and a second await is rejected at compile time as a moved-from read ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)); when the operand is **borrowed** (e.g. a `using var`-bound task), the second await cannot be statically prevented and raises `InvalidOperationException` at runtime.
- `OwningTask<T>` is a compile error when T's underlying (nullability-stripped) type is neither a class nor an interface type ([§14.4](#sec-owned-as-a-generic-argument)). The argument-type check is performed during type checking; the diagnostic identifies the rejected argument and points at [§14.4](#sec-owned-as-a-generic-argument).
- An `async` method, `async` lambda, or async iterator declares no borrow-bearing-record parameter, result, or element type ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods); [K2.1](#sec-kernel-k2) + [K6.1](#sec-kernel-k6)); `CancellationToken` is the single stdlib-certified exception (axiom [A10](#sec-axiom-register)); for generic async methods the check re-applies after substitution.
- No `ref`/`out` parameters on async methods, async lambdas, or iterators; no async lambda targets a function type with `ref`/`out` slots ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods); K2.1 + K6.1).
- An `await using var` of a class implementing `IAsyncDisposable` without a destructor (or of interface static type) is not live across a `yield return` in an async iterator ([§30.7](#sec-asynchronous-programming-async-iterators)).
- A borrow-bearing-record local does not cross a suspension point (`await`, `await using`, `await for`, or `yield return` in an iterator or async iterator — [§29.4](#sec-lazy-evaluation)) unless every borrow it carries has a frame-resident source ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods); K2.1 + K6.1).
- A blocking wait (`Wait()`, `Result` on an incomplete task) or blocking acquisition (`Mutex`/`Semaphore` `Acquire`/`TryAcquire(timeout)`, and the data-owning locks' blocking forms `Locked<T>.Lock()`/`TryLock(timeout)`, `RwLocked<T>.Read()`/`TryRead(timeout)`/`Write()`/`TryWrite(timeout)`) never **parks a thread** inside a domain continuation: the blocking forms are rejected at compile time in `async` bodies; where a continuation would actually park at runtime, `InvalidOperationException` is raised instead — completed-task reads and immediately-available acquisitions proceed ([§30.3](#sec-the-task-taskt-and-ownedtaskt-types), [§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization)).
- The task returned by invoking a call-bounded callback is awaited to settlement, on every path, before the callee returns — directly or via an aggregation helper over a purely-local collection; abandonment is an escape sink, and in a synchronous callee the invocation itself is rejected ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters); the minted task inherits the call bound to settlement — K6.1/[K6.4](#sec-kernel-k6); the synchronous-callee rejection derives: K6.3 + K3).
- A deferred-activation callee's plain function-typed parameter is retained only through frame residence — in the frame its call mints, bounded by that frame's life; every other retention past the call remains an escape sink, and a frame that carries the callback and escapes the callee other than by a deferred-activation return is an escape of the callback ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters); frame residence: K6.1 + K6.2).
- An unbound owned temporary is not passed as a plain argument to a deferred-activation or `Task`-family callee whose returned frame (or task) escapes the full expression ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries); [K6.5](#sec-kernel-k6) + K8.4).
- A `Task`-family call result is an owned production at the call site ([§28.3](#sec-producers)): `using var task := client.GetAsync(url);` binds an owned task — an obligation-assuming binding, not a [§28.10](#sec-using-var-initialized-from-a-borrow) pin — and [§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)'s named-owning-location admissions read accordingly. (K6.3; the family keying is axiom A2.)

<a id="sec-patterns-and-case"></a>
### C.7 Patterns and `case`

- A `_` arm appears at most once and is the last arm.
- A type-pattern `T` does not bind; a `var name: T` pattern binds.
- A type-pattern matches only non-null values; `null` matches only the `null` literal pattern, the `var` pattern, and `_`.
- `step` is not used in patterns; it is a range modifier only.
- A record-destructuring pattern's positional-binding count matches the record's positional-field count; the same arity rule applies to choice-case destructuring, and a payload-carrying case may not be matched bare ([§35.5](#sec-choice-matching)).
- A destructuring pattern's slot list is **positional or named, never mixed**; a named slot's identifier resolves against the pattern's type — a record's stored fields/auto-properties, a choice case's payload field names, or a class's public readable properties — and a named-slot binding is a borrow, a constant slot an `=` test, exactly as for the positional form ([§19.3](#sec-patterns)).
- A choice `case` with every declared case covered by an unguarded, irrefutable-slot arm is statically exhaustive with no `_` arm ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)); the marked owning-match scrutinee (`case move x of`) is a consume subject to the freeze ([K5](#sec-kernel-k5)), and guard evaluation in an owning match observes borrows, with transfer at arm selection ([§35.5](#sec-owning-match-guards)).
- Static exhaustiveness counts only **unguarded** arms; a `when`-guarded arm contributes nothing to the proof ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)).
- A `case` over a closed hierarchy whose root or any leaf is generic is **not proven** statically exhaustive by leaf coverage; it is completable only by an irrefutable arm — an unguarded `_` or an unguarded untyped `var` — and draws the non-exhaustiveness warning without one ([§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness-generic-leaves), v0.245).
- A statically exhaustive enum `case` cannot raise `MatchFailureException`: every producer of an enum value yields a declared value ([§5.4](#sec-enum-casts), [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis), [§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)), and the enum constants-coverage proof feeds [§21.7](#sec-the-return-statement)'s statement-`case` totality grant.
- Every class type named in a catch-arm pattern — bare, binding, or listed in a multi-type alternative — is `Exception` or a class deriving from it; an arm naming any other class type (`Object` included) is a compile error ([§31.2.1](#sec-arm-patterns)).
- A multi-type catch alternative in **binding** form types the binding as the listed types' **nearest common base** — with every listed type `Exception`-derived, always `Exception` or a class deriving from it ([§31.2.1](#sec-arm-patterns)).
- A generic type parameter used as a catch-arm type must carry an **`Exception`-derived class bound** (`where TEx: Exception`, or a class deriving from it); an unconstrained, value-constrained, or `where TEx: class`-only parameter, or one bounded by a class outside the `Exception` family, is a compile error, checked at the generic declaration ([§31.2.1](#sec-arm-patterns)).

<a id="sec-appendix-c-serialization"></a>
<a id="sec-appendix-c-serialization-synthesis"></a>
### C.8 Serialization synthesis

- A type declaring `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable` ([§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)) that is not serialization-eligible is a compile error **at the conformance declaration**, naming the first offending member.
- A record's serialized components are value-shaped only (primitive/`string`/enum/eligible record/value-like eligible choice/`T?`/non-owning inline array — [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)'s record-admissibility); a class-, interface-, `Shared<T>`-, `Weak<T>`-, or heap-collection-typed serialized component makes a record ineligible (compile error at the conformance declaration). Positional and body records agree.
- A class enters serialization synthesis by declaring `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable`; its serialized shape is read from the field types (`owned`/value → owning edge, `Shared<T>` → identity participant, `Weak<T>` and plain borrow → back-edge), with no header shape clause.
- `Shared<T>`/`Weak<T>` are serialization-eligible when `T` is a serialization-eligible class; a `Shared<T>` serializes by identity (the tag keyed on the underlying value `Get()` borrows, reconstructed by `Clone()`), a `Weak<T>` as a back-reference (reconstructed by `Downgrade()`). A cycle closes through a nullable `Weak<T>?` back-edge on a `Shared<T>` spine — ordinary ownership-valid construction, no two-phase window.
- Identity is preserved on deserialization (a `$ref` binds to the already-reconstructed object, never duplicated). A `Weak<T>` reference whose target is never strongly reached anywhere in the graph raises `SerializationException` at deserialization.
- A `polymorphic` registry (a class-body member) is closed: each discriminator is a unique non-empty string literal, each registered type must be assignable to the declaring class and itself type-driven serialization-eligible (compile error at the registry otherwise); an unregistered discriminator (read) or unregistered run-time type (write) raises `SerializationException`. No reflective subtype discovery.
- `serialized` and its in-clause words `skip`, `optional` are contextual (the field-name clause); `polymorphic` is contextual in the class-member registry position ([Appendix B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords)).

<a id="sec-appendix-c-ffi"></a>
### C.9 FFI

- `extern` methods appear only inside `extern` blocks.
- `extern` declarations have no body.
- `extern` method signatures use only FFI-compatible types ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)).
- Empty `extern` blocks are rejected.
- `ref`/`out` on extern parameters are admitted only for FFI-pointee scalars and C-compatible records ([§32.5](#sec-boundary-out-ref)); `owned`, `out owned`, and `scoped` extern parameters are rejected.
- Nullable extern forms are exactly `CString?`/`WString?`/`RawBytes?` and nullable FFI function types; nullable value types are rejected at the boundary ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)).
- An inline-array extern argument is an assignable storage location; `[N]T` extern returns are rejected ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)).
- `RawBytes` occupies two C slots in parameter positions; `RawBytes` extern returns are rejected ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)).
- A callback argument of an extern call may not capture a binding that is an `out` argument of the same call ([§32.5](#sec-boundary-out-ref)).
- `Ptr<T>`'s pointee is gated per-instantiation to the FFI-pointee set; `Ptr<Ptr<U>>` is rejected ([§32.12](#sec-foreign-memory)). The C-compatible property is computed per [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) and named in diagnostics ([§32.13](#sec-c-compatible-records)); the single-field direct admission requires exactly one integer-or-pointer scalar field.
- `env` pairing is well-formed: at most one `env` marker per extern declaration, paired with exactly one function-typed parameter containing exactly one `env` position; `env` does not combine with `variadic(N)`; capture-bearing callback arguments are admitted only at the paired parameter ([§32.8](#sec-callbacks)).
- `variadic(N)` requires N ≤ the declared arity and rides the `symbol` clause; variadic-position parameter types are drawn from the promoted set, and the diagnostic for a non-promoted type names the type to declare ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)).
- `Interop.CodeAddress<F>`'s argument satisfies the static callback admission; `F` is gated per-instantiation to FFI-compatible function types ([§32.8](#sec-callbacks)).

<a id="sec-operators"></a>
### C.10 Operators

- `=` and `<>` are not overloaded on classes.
- An operator overload is `public static` and at least one parameter is the declaring type ([§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)).
- Operator parameters carry no parameter modifiers (`ref`/`out`/`owned`/`scoped` are rejected semantically); `owned` may appear only on an operator's return type ([§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)).
- A record/enum overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` also declares `Equals(T)` and `GetHashCode` — on a record, `override GetHashCode`; on an enum, a plain `GetHashCode(): int`, since enum members never carry `override` (the [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions) co-declaration rule; enum spelling).
- Comparison operators are overloaded as a complete group (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` together; `=` and `<>` together).
- The bitwise complement operator is `~`; the boolean negation operator is `not`. They are not interchangeable. `~` is user-overloadable; `not` is not.
- Assignment and compound-assignment operators (`:=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `mod=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `??=`) are not user-overloadable. The `+=` and `-=` event-subscription forms on `EventSource<T>`, `AsyncEventSource<T>`, and `SharedEventSource<T>` are a fixed compiler desugaring ([§17.2](#sec-notes-on-operators)), not operator overloads.

<a id="sec-static-initialization"></a>
### C.11 Static initialization

- Cyclic static initialization across **distinct** types is rejected at compile time when visible to the [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order) dependency approximation (static-member references between distinct types, followed transitively through statically-resolvable calls within the compilation unit); a cycle the approximation misses raises a runtime-synthesized `TypeInitializationException` (`InnerException` null) at the same-thread **re-entrant** touch — one arriving from outside the touched type's own initialization — and partially-initialized statics are never observed through a re-entrant touch. Within-type forward reads of later `static readonly` fields are rejected transitively through the same call set; the routes both approximations miss are recorded residuals with the checked-mode watermark bound ([§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)).
- A type's static initializer runs exactly once process-wide; a cross-domain touch of a type mid-initialization blocks until initialization completes or observes the failed state ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) rule 1).
- A mutable (non-`readonly`, non-`const`) static field or auto-property has one of [§22.12](#sec-static-members) rule 2's admitted forms: an internally-synchronized handle type — a type declaring the **synchronized** and not the **displacement-unbounded** fact (stdlib §1): `Mutex`, `Semaphore`, `Atomic<T>`, `AtomicInteger<T>`, `ChannelSender<T>`, `SharedEventSource<T>` (`Channel<T>` declares no facts and is excluded) — a `Task?`/`Task<T>?` lazy cache, or — admitted with the rule's declaration-site warning — a primitive/enum/heap-free-inline-array value static (form (iii)) or an owning-inline-array static field (`[N owned]T?`/`[N owned]T`, form (iv), disposal per [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)); anything else is rejected.
- `static readonly` and `const` of immutable content are unrestricted; a `static readonly` field of class or interface type outside rule 4's warning-suppression set — the types declaring the **synchronized** or the **immutable** fact (stdlib §1): the six form-(i) types (`SharedEventSource<T>` included), `Locked<T>`, `RwLocked<T>`, and `FrozenArray<T>` — draws the [§22.12](#sec-static-members) rule 4 declaration-site warning.
- A handler argument at any call resolving to a subscribe position declared on `ISharedEvent<T>` or `SharedEventSource<T>` is compiler-checked **capture-free** — a non-capturing lambda or a static method reference ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)'s stdlib-stated capture-free register; [§22.12](#sec-static-members) rule 5) — and method-reference formation over a capture-free-register position is rejected ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)), making the admission hold at every site, aliases included; shared-event subscriber lists are internally synchronized (stdlib §6.5).
- The access that triggers a failing static initialization, and every subsequent access, observe the same cached `TypeInitializationException`; the original exception is observable only as its `InnerException` ([§22.7](#sec-constructors)).
- A `const` declaration's initializer is a constant expression ([§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions)); an initializer whose compile-time evaluation faults (overflow, division by zero) is rejected at the declaration, never deferred to runtime.

<a id="sec-entry-point"></a>
### C.12 Entry point

- An executable build's root compilation ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly)) defines exactly one qualifying `Main` method, or `--main-class` ([§33.5](#sec-program-entry-point-resolution)) selects one when several classes qualify; a qualifying `Main` in a dependency artifact is inert — an ordinary method, never a candidate, never a conflict ([§33.1](#sec-the-main-method)).
- A class declares at most one qualifying `Main`; multiple qualifying overloads in the same class are rejected at compile time without flag-based override.
- `Main` is `public static`. If `async`, its return type is `Task`, `Task<int>`, or one of the parameterized forms; otherwise it returns `()` or `int`.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-modules"></a>
### C.13 Module identity and program assembly

- Every module in a program is the product of exactly one compilation; no source file joins a module by declaring its name, and `internal` access is closed by the declaring module's compilation — including between co-members of an SCC unit ([§2.8.1](#sec-module-identity-and-closure)).
- A build whose artifact set contains two distinct artifacts declaring the same module name — or an artifact declaring a module name the implementation provides — is rejected, naming both origins; bit-identical duplicate presentations are deduplicated, not diagnosed ([§2.8.1](#sec-module-identity-and-closure) rules 3/5).
- An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is a compile error ([§2.8.1](#sec-module-identity-and-closure) rule 4).
- A build missing a member of the dependency closure — including modules referenced only from declaration bodies carried in an interface — is an error naming the missing module ([§2.8.3](#sec-transitive-closure-and-type-identity) rule 1).
- Naming a transitively-reachable type in source requires importing its declaring module; using its values does not ([§2.8.3](#sec-transitive-closure-and-type-identity) rule 2).
- Disagreeing descriptions of one type in a build's closure (a stale artifact) are a build error naming the artifacts ([§2.8.3](#sec-transitive-closure-and-type-identity) rule 3).
- Presenting an executable artifact as a dependency is a build error naming the artifact and its kind ([§2.8.4](#sec-program-assembly) rule 4).
- A member's contract records — clause kind, `static` qualifier, canonical text, recorded tier — and a class's `invariant` records agree across all descriptions of a type in a build's closure; disagreement is the rule-3 staleness error ([§2.8.2](#sec-artifact-interface), [§2.8.3](#sec-transitive-closure-and-type-identity)).
- A contract record's recorded tier is the clause's [§22.16](#sec-contract-tiers) tier, a declaration fact (the `static` qualifier; the constant-fold prover floor), never what a particular compilation opportunistically discharged at a body or call site ([§2.8.2](#sec-artifact-interface)).

---

### C.14 Purity

- `pure` combines with neither `async` nor `yield`; destructors, static constructors, `extern` declarations, and auto-properties carry no `pure`.
- A pure member declares no `ref`/`out`/`out owned`/`owned`/`scoped` parameter, no move-only value parameter or return ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types), v0.230/v0.234), and no `owned` class-typed return.
- A pure body contains no store whose target root leaves the frame, no disposal-running or owned-consuming operation, no class construction outside the throw carve-out, no invocation of a function-typed value, no enumerator-constructing `for`, and no call to a member not pure-declared or pure-classified ([§22.15](#sec-pure-body-rules)).
- The throw-carve-out operand's class is trivial-dispose and its invoked constructor pure ([§22.15](#sec-pure-throw)); the dispose-after-arm on such an operand is the compiler-inserted flag-setting free, running no user code ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types), [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)).
- Overrides and implementations of pure members restate `pure`; purity never narrows down an override chain ([§22.15](#sec-pure-dispatch)).
- Field initializers of a pure-constructed class and default-value expressions of pure members' parameters satisfy the pure-body rules.

### C.15 Contract clauses

- A contract clause's expression is `bool`, satisfies the [§22.15](#sec-pure-members) pure-body rules, and contains no `throw`, no `await`, no store, and no owned-consuming or disposal-running operation.
- `requires` evaluates after argument binding and before the chain/initializers/body, in declaration order, and is never elided unless proven; `ensures` evaluates on every normal-completion path after result and `out`-slot binding and before scope-end disposals, and never on a throw path.
- `result` appears only in `ensures` of a member with a declared return type and is a borrow position; each `old` operand evaluates exactly once at entry after `requires`, by copy for value/record/enum/`string` and as a frame-resident borrow for class/interface types, under the ordinary [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows) binding rules.
- An override or implementation declares no `requires` and may add `ensures`; inherited clauses are never restated; multi-root `requires` combines by disjunction, `ensures` by conjunction.
- A `static`-qualified clause the active prover cannot discharge at its discharge site (declaring body for `ensures`/`invariant`; each call site for `requires`) is a compile error; a `static requires` mentions only caller-visible state; a constant clause folding `false` is a compile error.
- The class invariant is evaluated at most-derived-construction exit, public-method entry/exit, and public-setter entry/exit — never on non-public members, destructors, `Dispose`, throw paths, or `this`-receiver calls.
- Clauses never distinguish overloads; `invariant` members appear only in classes; `old`/`result` appear only where the rules above admit them.

<a id="appendix-d-conformance-levels"></a>
## Appendix D: Conformance Levels

**Diagnostic identity.** This specification mandates *when* a diagnostic is produced (accept / warn / reject) and, in places, what it should name; it deliberately defines **no error-code registry or message taxonomy**. Diagnostic identity — codes, exact wording, formatting — is implementation-defined, and conformance claims about diagnostics classify outcomes only (a mandated rejection is satisfied by any error at the mandated site; a mandated warning by any warning). A future revision may introduce a code registry if multiple implementations materialize; until then, requiring exact messages would freeze prose this document revises freely.

This specification defines two conformance levels. The partition exists so that an implementation can be *complete and sound for a well-defined inner language* before the outer features are attempted, and so that the test-suite and teaching material can follow the same boundary.

<a id="sec-the-levels"></a>
### D.1 The levels

- **Core conformance.** An implementation conforms at the Core level when it implements every normative rule of this specification *except* the Extended features listed in D.2, and *rejects* — with a diagnostic naming the construct and the feature — any program that uses an Extended feature it does not implement. Silent misbehavior on Extended input is non-conforming; clean rejection is the Core-conforming response.
- **Full conformance.** An implementation conforms at the Full level when it implements the entire specification: Core plus every Extended feature.

An implementation may also conform at "Core plus named features" (e.g., *Core + Events + FFI*), implementing some Extended features and rejecting the rest; a conformance claim of this form names the features implemented.

<a id="sec-extended-features"></a>
### D.2 The Extended features

| Feature | Specification sections | Standard-library sections |
|---|---|---|
| **Events** | the event-subscription desugaring of [§17.2](#sec-notes-on-operators) | stdlib [§6.5](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-events-ievent-eventsource) entire — `EventSource<T>`, `IEvent<T>`, `AsyncEventSource<T>`, `IAsyncEvent<T>`, `ISharedEvent<T>`, `SharedEventSource<T>` — plus `Subscription` (stdlib [§2.11](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-subscription)) |
| **Asynchronous programming** | [§30](#sec-asynchronous-programming) entire — including domains, spawning, and channels ([§30.13](#sec-runtime-model)–[§30.15](#sec-channels)); [§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal) (`await using`, `IAsyncDisposable`); the async-iterator forms of [§29](#sec-iteration-2) (`IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerator<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerator<T>`) | `Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, completion sources, `CancellationToken`/`CancellationTokenSource`, `Mutex`/`Semaphore`/`Atomic<T>`, `Domain`, `Channel<T>`/`ChannelSender<T>`, the async forms of IO and sequence operations |
| **Serialization synthesis** | [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis) | stdlib §2.14–2.15 |
| **Foreign Function Interface** | [§32](#sec-foreign-function-interface); the FFI clauses of [§15.1.3](#sec-inline-array-ffi); the C-compatible row and reservation-clause exception of [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) | `Ptr<T>`, `Interop` (stdlib §10.5–§10.6); `RawBytes.FromForeign`, `CString`/`WString.Pointer` (stdlib §10.1–§10.3); `OwningBuffer<T>.DangerousPointer` (stdlib §4.14) |
| **Buffers and spans** | the buffer/span clauses of [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership) (`move` on `OwningBuffer`/`Span` slots) | stdlib §3.3, §4.14–4.16 |
| **Contract proving** | the extended prover fragment of [§22.16](#sec-contract-tiers) (linear integer arithmetic, null-test flow, closed-set case analysis) — what gives the `static` clause qualifier reach beyond the constant-and-`when`-clause floor; a Core implementation **rejects** a `static` clause it cannot discharge (D.1's clean rejection), never downgrading a demanded proof to a runtime check | — |
| **Sequence operations (LINQ-style)** | — | stdlib §5 entire |
| **Shared ownership** | [§28.13](#sec-shared-ownership) | `Shared<T>`, `Weak<T>` (stdlib §2.16) |
| **Move-only value types (owning inline arrays, owning choices)** | [§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays) and the `owned` slot marker of Appendix A.5's `InlineArrayType`; [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types); the owning choice classification and its clauses — the `owned` payload marker's owning reading, the owning match ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)–[§35.5](#sec-owning-match)), the drop-on-overwrite rule, and the transfer-closure field clause of [§35.12](#sec-choice-sendability); the move-only discard clause of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_); the owning-inline-array field clauses of [§28.5](#sec-owned-fields) (including the double-marking rejection) and [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order); the move-only clause of [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields); the move-only row of [§28.11](#sec-element-slot-policy)'s element-category table; the owned-slot clauses of [§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for)'s inline-array desugaring and the move-only paragraph of [§29.8](#sec-iterators-with-owned-parameters); the move-only instantiation checks of [§7.10](#sec-generics-and-nullability) and [§14.2](#sec-constraints) (`where T: value`) | — |

Everything not listed is **Core**: lexical structure through generics, records, enums, classes, interfaces, inheritance, nullability, patterns and `case`, expressions and statements, operators and overloading, properties and indexers, the entire ownership system of [§28](#sec-resource-management) (except §28.12, §28.13, and the move-only value-type clauses of §28.5, §28.7, and §28.11 carved to the **Move-only value types** row above), synchronous iteration ([§29](#sec-iteration-2)'s non-async forms, including iterator methods and `IOwningEnumerable<T>`), exceptions ([§31](#sec-exception-handling)), the entry point, and the corresponding standard-library sections.

<a id="sec-feature-dependencies"></a>
### D.3 Dependencies and closure

- Extended features depend on Core; Core depends on no Extended feature. The Core sections' references *into* Extended sections (e.g., [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)'s notes on async lambdas, [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s span examples) are normative only for implementations of the referenced feature.
- The async-iterator forms belong to **Asynchronous programming** and additionally require synchronous iteration (Core). **Buffers and spans**, **Sequence operations**, and **Shared ownership** depend only on Core. **Events**' async event source requires **Asynchronous programming**; the synchronous `EventSource<T>` does not, and neither do `ISharedEvent<T>`/`SharedEventSource<T>`: their capture-free admission is ordinary [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters) typing, and in a single-domain build the synchronization guarantee is satisfied vacuously; the deferred shared-async twin, if ever shipped, requires Asynchronous programming like `AsyncEventSource<T>`.
- **Move-only value types** depend only on Core (value-like and borrow-bearing choices are Core; only the owning classification is this row's), and no other Extended feature depends on them: **Buffers and spans** does not (`OwningBuffer<T>`, `Span<T>`, and `ReadOnlySpan<T>` reject move-only element types, [§14.4](#sec-owned-as-a-generic-argument)); **Asynchronous programming** *references* them — [§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)'s transfer-closure rule 2 admits an owning-inline-array field, and [§30.1](#sec-async-methods)'s frame rule covers move-only parameters — but does not depend on them: an Extended section's references into another Extended feature's clauses are normative only for implementations of both features, the first bullet's rule for Core-section references into Extended sections generalized to Extended-to-Extended references.
- A Core implementation's standard library omits the types of unimplemented Extended features entirely (they are absent, not stubbed); programs referencing them fail name resolution with the feature-naming diagnostic of D.1.

<a id="sec-conformance-and-the-runtime-model"></a>
### D.4 Conformance and the runtime model

The execution-domain guarantees of [§30.13](#sec-runtime-model) are stated within the Asynchronous-programming feature, but their soundness consequences for [§28](#sec-resource-management) hold trivially in a Core implementation: with no `async`/`await`, every program is a single continuation in a single domain. A Core implementation therefore satisfies the domain guarantees by construction.
